It avoids wasting computation on stable positions and prematurely committing unstable ones.

entry.title: Last But Not Least: Boundary Attention CalibratiON for Multimodal KV Cache Compression

author.name: Tianhao Chen, Yuheng Wu, Kelu Yao, Xiaogang Xu, Xiaobin Hu, Dongman Lee

entry.summary: BACON is a plug-and-play multimodal KV cache compression method that calibrates observation-window attention with last-query evidence to recover answer-critical visual tokens, suppressing isolated noise via intra-layer coherence and inter-layer persistence. It addresses how aggressive compression dilutes sparse visual evidence in MLLMs.

entry.title: S1-DeepResearch: Beyond Search, Toward Real-World Long-Horizon Research Agents

author.name: Yao Dong, Xinglin Xiao, Liwei Dong, Xinlong Jin, Zhengbo Li, Heng Zhang, Duyun Wang, Nan Xu

entry.summary: S1-DeepResearch proposes a unified trajectory construction paradigm for training deep research agents that goes beyond search-centric closed-ended QA to cover evidence integration, knowledge synthesis, planning, file understanding, and structured report generation. It targets real-world long-horizon research tasks. Relevant to the active deep-research-agent area.

entry.title: State-Grounded Multi-Agent Synthetic Data Generation for Tool-Augmented LLMs

author.name: Rahul Khedar, Eshita, Sneha Teja Sree Reddy Thondapu, Mayank Malhotra, Arup Das, Jitesh Chandra, Yun-Shiuan Chuang, Chaitanya Kulkarni, Arun Menon, Linsey Pang, Avinash Karn, Mouli V, Prakhar Mehrotra

entry.summary: StateGen is a synthetic data generation platform for tool-augmented LLM agents that orchestrates a four-role LLM loop (user simulator, agent under test, state-grounded tool simulator, multi-axis judge) with an authoritative state manager enforcing a backend-is-truth invariant to eliminate tool-call hallucinations. It produces scored, reasoning-rich multi-turn training conversations. Useful for training tool-using agents at scale.

entry.title: GeoDisaster: Benchmarking Orchestrated Agents for Operational Disaster Geo-Intelligence

author.name: Maram Hasan, Aman Verma, Savitra Roy, Hariseetharam Gunduboina, Daksh Jain, Muhammad Haris Khan, Subhasis Chaudhuri, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: GeoDisaster is an operational geospatial disaster reasoning benchmark with 2,921 verified instances across 43 question types and five task families, integrating heterogeneous EO/GIS evidence including optical and SAR imagery, masks, vectors, road networks, and exposure layers for tool-grounded spatial reasoning. It pushes RS-VLMs toward operational geo-intelligence. A substantive benchmark for disaster response AI.

entry.title: Qwen-RobotNav Technical Report: A Scalable Navigation Model Designed for an Agentic Navigation System

author.name: Jiazhao Zhang, Gengze Zhou, Hale Yin, Yiyang Huang, Zixing Lei, Qihang Peng, Haoqi Yuan, Jie Zhang, Xudong Guo, Xiaoyue Chen, An Yang, Fei Huang, Junyang Lin, Dayiheng Liu, Jingren Zhou, Zhuoyuan Yu, Jingyang Fan, Zhixuan Liang, Pei Lin, Ye Wang, Anzhe Chen, Kun Yan, Xiao Xu, Jiahao Li, Lulu Hu, Minying Zhang, Shurui Li, Wenhu Xiao, Shuai Bai, Xuancheng Ren, Chenxu Lv, Chenfei Wu, Xiong-Hui Chen

entry.summary: Qwen-RobotNav is a scalable navigation model with an externally reconfigurable observation strategy, exposing task modes and controllable observation parameters (token budget, per-camera weights) for an agentic navigation system. Training-time randomization enables inference-time behavior control across navigation tasks.

entry.title: EgoInfinity: A Web-Scale 4D Hand-Object Interaction Data Engine for Any-View Robot Retargeting and Video-to-Action Robot Learning

author.name: Gaotian Wang, Kejia Ren, Andrew Morgan, Yiting Chen, Howard H. Qian, Podshara Chanrungmaneekul, Kaiyu Hang

entry.summary: EgoInfinity is a universal 4D hand-object interaction data engine that converts arbitrary internet RGB videos into actionable robot training data via perception, segmentation, reconstruction, refinement, and retargeting without human annotation. It enables web-scale data generation for robot retargeting and video-to-action learning.

entry.title: Can LLMs Be CEOs? Benchmarking Strategic Resource Reallocation with Multi-Role Agent Simulation

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Xueqing Peng, Lingfei Qian, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: Introduces CEO-Bench, a multi-agent benchmark evaluating LLMs on executive strategic resource reallocation under conflicting stakeholder recommendations, information asymmetry, and temporal dependencies. Moves beyond isolated cognitive tasks toward realistic decision integration.

entry.title: Closing the Feedback Loop: From Experience Extraction to Insight Governance in Verbal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanwei Cui, Xing Zhang, Yulong Zhang, Li Shao, Xiaofeng Shi, Guanghui Wang, Peiyang He

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free verbal reinforcement learning framework with insight governance to handle the retention-forgetting dilemma in non-stationary environments. Identifies four requirements (outcome-driven evaluation, persistent evidence, non-monotonic lifecycle, compositional governance) for managing learned verbal rules.

entry.title: DiagFlowBench: Evaluating How Language Models Handle Off-Procedure Inputs in Grounded Diagnostic Dialogue

author.name: Guillermo Gil de Avalle, Laura Maruster, Shaina Raza, Christos Emmanouilidis

entry.summary: Introduces DiagFlowBench, evaluating how grounded diagnostic-dialogue LLMs handle off-procedure, out-of-scope inputs across 50 industrial flowcharts and 1,676 conversations. Reveals high variability in abstention rates among ten models when users stray from approved procedural steps.

entry.title: LLM Consumer Behavior Theory: Foundations of a Novel Research Field

author.name: Manon Reusens, Sofie Goethals, David Martens

entry.summary: Introduces LLM Consumer Behavior Theory as a new field analyzing how LLM agents make consumption decisions on behalf of users and how these aggregate into market demand. Unifies fragmented literature on LLM decision-making, human simulation, and preference modeling.

entry.title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications

author.name: Divyansh Srivastava, Shreya Ghosh, Anshul Verma, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent healthcare framework using deterministic orchestration constraints instead of LLM-as-judge routing, with a neuro-symbolic state-tracking gate enforcing the OLDCARTS clinical protocol to prevent premature diagnostic handoff and silent hallucinations. Targets safer medical conversational reasoning.

entry.title: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding

author.name: Jingyuan Huang, Zuming Huang, Yucheng Shi, Tianze Yang, Xiaoming Zhai, Wei Chu, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for VLM-based GUI grounding, addressing how naive on-policy self-distillation degrades when student-generated prefixes deviate from target coordinates. Improves precise screen-coordinate prediction for small UI elements in high-resolution screenshots.

entry.title: DRFLOW: A Deep Research Benchmark for Personalized Workflow Prediction

author.name: Md Tawkat Islam Khondaker, Raymond Li, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed, Laks V. S. Lakshmanan, Issam H. Laradji

entry.summary: Introduces DRFLOW, a deep-research benchmark for personalized workflow prediction where agents must identify concrete action-step sequences from scattered heterogeneous sources rather than generate reports. Targets enterprise tasks requiring procedural answers.

entry.title: EvolveNav: Proactive Preflection and Self-Evolving Memory for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Qi Chai, Wenhao Shen, Nanjie Yao, Yue Xia, Kaiyong Zhao, Jie Ma, Guosheng Lin, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving zero-shot object-goal navigation framework that builds an agentic rule memory from past trajectories, retrieves rules via upper confidence bound balancing relevance and success, and forecasts failures through a memory-guided preflection module. Enables continuous test-time improvement without prior training.

entry.title: The Price of Anarchy in Disaggregated Inference

author.name: Athos Georgiou (NCA)

entry.summary: Provides a game-theoretic analysis of disaggregated LLM inference, modeling separated prefill and decode GPU pools as three coupled games (resource, caching, congestion) using NVIDIA Dynamo as a case study. Characterizes how GPU saturation induces regime transitions affecting payoffs.

entry.title: ANEForge: Python for direct computation on the Apple Neural Engine

author.name: Spencer H. Bryngelson

entry.summary: Presents ANEForge, a Python package that compiles a lazy tensor graph into a single program running directly on the Apple Neural Engine without CoreML, exposing native fused attention and streaming int8/int4/sparse weights. Removes CoreML's silent fallback that lets the ANE go unused.

entry.title: LiveStarPro: Proactive Streaming Video Understanding with Hierarchical Memory for Long-Horizon Streams

author.name: Zhenyu Yang, Kairui Zhang, Bing Wang, Shengsheng Qian, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: Presents a proactive streaming video assistant that decides when to respond and maintains hierarchical memory over long-horizon streams, using single-pass perplexity verification for response timing. Aims to mitigate forgetting and improve real-time responsiveness in Video-LLMs.

entry.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale

author.name: Maksim Shaposhnikov, Nicolas Fortuin, Simon Stipcich, Maria I. Gorinova, Amy Heineike, Rob Willoughby

entry.summary: Proposes a framework letting skill authors construct realistic tasks to evaluate individual agent skills, applied at scale to 500 real-world skills generating 1,000 tasks with scoring rubrics. Addresses the lack of reusable methodology for assessing reusable agent knowledge artifacts.

entry.title: PearlVLA: Progressive Embodied Action-Plan Refinement in Latent Space

author.name: Bochen Yang, Lianlei Shan

entry.summary: Proposes PearlVLA, a vision-language-action framework that moves deliberation into the latent space of a VLM, separating fixed visual grounding from an iterative latent planning branch that queries a frozen latent world model. Seeks the planning benefits of explicit reasoning without its latency.

entry.title: Half a Link can Be Enough to Predict a Whole Link: Understanding Generalization in Knowledge Graph Foundation Models

author.name: Cosimo Gregucci, Obaidah Theeb, Daniel Hernandez, Antonio Vergari, Steffen Staab

entry.summary: This paper analyzes generalization in knowledge graph foundation models, showing that observing a half-link (h,r) or (r,t) often suffices to predict a full test triple. It yields a taxonomy of four generalization scenarios via stratified analysis.

entry.title: Neuron Level Analysis of Large Language Model in Legal Domain Reasoning

author.name: Eri Onami, Youmi Ma, Shuhei Kurita, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: Performs neuron-level analysis of legal-domain reasoning across seven open-weight LLMs, using neuron attribution to identify influential neurons whose suppression collapses target-task accuracy while random suppression does not. It finds a small cross-task neuron subset plus genuinely task-specific neurons, with legal benchmarks showing high overlap.

entry.title: Formalize Once, Edit the Rest: Efficient Lean-Based Answer Selection for Math Reasoning

author.name: Ji Feng, Zhouxing Shi

entry.summary: BASE is a base-and-edit pipeline for Lean-based answer selection in math reasoning that formalizes one base candidate per problem and derives the remaining candidates by editing answers, reducing the cost of autoformalizing each candidate independently. It targets efficient test-time scaling with formal verification.

entry.title: Who Should Lead Decoding Now? Tracking Reliable Trajectories for Ensembling Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Heecheol Yun, Joonhyung Park, Joowon Kim, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: This work investigates decoding dynamics of masked diffusion language models, finding that successful generations show stable confidence over answer-relevant positions, and proposes TIE, a trajectory-based iterative ensembling framework for fusing knowledge across MDLMs. It relays promising intermediate states between models to correct unreliable trajectories.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Personalization via Semantic Constraint Verification

author.name: Xuran Li, Guanqin Zhang, Imran Razzak, Hakim Hacid, Eleanna Kafeza, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: NLICV is a scalable framework for evaluating LLM personalization by mapping sentence meanings to truth-condition sets verified via a natural language inference model, categorizing behaviors into personalization, generalization, sycophancy, and failure. It aims to replace brittle surface-matching and expensive LLM-judge metrics.

entry.title: How Far Can Machine Translation Quality Take You? Extrinsic Discourse Evaluation in Goal-Oriented Setups

author.name: Wafaa Mohammed, Kata Naszadi, Vlad Niculae

entry.summary: This work performs extrinsic discourse evaluation of machine translation under static and interactive regimes, using an entity counting task and the goal-oriented Welfare Diplomacy game. It shows high intrinsic MT quality does not reliably predict downstream discourse success, with strong systems still producing referential inconsistencies.

entry.title: DEEPRUBRIC: Evidence-Tree Rubric Supervision for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Deep Research Agents

author.name: Minghang Zhu, Chuyang Wei, Junhao Xu, Yilin Cheng, Zhumin Chen, Jiyan He

entry.summary: ASRD is a training-free framework for diffusion LLMs that operates in embedding space to decouple decoding context into trusted and untrusted tokens via anchor tokens, mitigating error propagation and local error reinforcement in revocable decoding. It guides parallel generation while preserving quality.

entry.title: Re-feeding Is Not Replaying: Measuring Replay Noise in Counterfactual Token-Credit Estimation

author.name: Nils Matteson

entry.summary: This paper measures the noise introduced by the common practice of re-feeding transcript prefixes (rather than replaying from cached KV state) in per-token counterfactual credit estimation for LLM rollouts. Using a three-pass design, it shows re-feeding meaningfully changes outcomes at low-margin decision tokens. Important methodological caution for credit-assignment and interpretability work.

entry.title: VisualClaw: A Real-Time, Personalized Agent for the Physical World

author.name: Haoqin Tu, Jianwen Chen, Zijun Wang, Siwei Han, Juncheng Wu, Hardy Chen, Haonian Ji, Kaiwen Xiong, Jiaqi Liu, Peng Xia, Jieru Mei, Hongliang Fei, Jason Eshraghian, Zeyu Zheng, Yuyin Zhou, Huaxiu Yao, Cihang Xie

entry.summary: VisualClaw is a self-evolving multimodal agent for the physical world using hybrid encoding to reduce latency by filtering uninformative streaming frames and compressing the text skill bank, plus a skill-evolution mechanism that learns from failures via retrieved memories. It addresses VLM deployment gaps in latency, static scaffolds, and tool-using evaluation. Relevant to real-time embodied agents.

entry.title: Training LLMs with Reinforcement Learning over Digital Twin Representations for Reasoning-Intensive Surgical VideoQA

author.name: Yiqing Shen, Han Zhang, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: This RL framework trains LLMs to decouple perception from reasoning for surgical video QA by operating over digital twin representations built from surgical foundation models, with hierarchical frame, temporal-window, and procedure-level representations and probabilistic uncertainty estimates. It addresses how token compression fragments spatial-temporal relationships and limits multi-step reasoning. A novel structured approach to surgical VideoQA.

entry.title: Future Dynamic 3D Reconstruction: A 3D World Model with Disentangled Ego-Motion

author.name: Nils Morbitzer, Jonathan Evers, Artem Savkin, Thomas Stauner, Nassir Navab, Federico Tombari, Stefano Gasperini

entry.summary: FR3D is a 3D world model predicting persistent 3D latent representations for future dynamic reconstruction, explicitly disentangling scene evolution from ego-motion treated as a latent action proxy. This addresses physical inconsistencies like morphing/vanishing objects in 2D video world models.

entry.title: MuseVLA: An Adaptive Multimodal Sensing Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Xingyuming Liu, Ruichun Ma, Heyu Guo, Qixiu Li, Qingwen Yang, Lin Luo, Shiqi Jiang, Chenren Xu, Jiaolong Yang, Baining Guo

entry.summary: MuseVLA is an adaptive multimodal sensing vision-language-action model that invokes novel sensors (temperature, sound, radar) on demand as tool calls during robotic manipulation. It generates sensor tokens to select which modality to engage, extending beyond RGB-only VLA models.

entry.title: ACE-Ego-0: Unifying Egocentric Human and Robotic Data for VLA Pretraining

author.name: Hao Li, Ganlong Zhao, Yufei Liu, Haotian Hou, Guoquan Ye, Tongyan Fang, Chunxiao Liu, Siyuan Huang, Jianbo Liu, Xiaogang Wang, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: ACE-Ego-0 is a unified VLA pretraining framework jointly leveraging egocentric human videos and robot data, with a scalable video-to-action pipeline converting human videos into robot-format pseudo-actions. It addresses divergences in action spaces and embodiment between human and robot data.

entry.title: EBench: Elemental Diagnosis of Generalist Mobile Manipulation Policies

author.name: Ning Gao, Jinliang Zheng, Xing Gao, Haoxiang Ma, Hanqing Wang, Yukai Wang, Jiantong Chen, Zanxin Chen, Shujie Zhang, Mingda Jia, Xuekun Jiang, Zihou Zhu, Xinyu Li, Shuai Wang, Hao Li, Wenzhe Cai, Yuqiang Yang, Xudong Xu, Zhaoyang Lyu, Yao Mu, Tai Wang, Jiangmiao Pang, Jia Zeng, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: EBench is a simulation benchmark that diagnoses generalist mobile manipulation policies across 5 capability and 4 generalization dimensions over 26 tasks, evaluating models like pi-0, pi-0.5, XVLA, and InternVLA-A1 beyond a single success-rate scalar. It reveals that similar success rates hide strikingly different capability profiles.

entry.title: Quantifying Consistency in LLM Logical Reasoning via Structural Uncertainty

author.name: Baishali Chaudhury, Mengdie Flora Wang, Hyunji Hayley Park, Rahul Ghosh, Sungmin Hong, Jae Oh Woo

entry.summary: Proposes structural uncertainty, a consistency-aware framework measuring whether LLMs can stably rank competing reasoning candidates via self-preference pairwise judgments. Aims to complement output-dispersion-based reliability assessment in multi-step deductive reasoning.

entry.title: A Machine-Learned Comorbidity Index

author.name: Suleman Baloch, Kishlay Jha, Alberto M. Segre, Philip M. Polgreen, Bijaya Adhikari

entry.summary: Proposes a Machine-Learned Comorbidity Index that maps diagnosis codes to a scalar by maximizing normalized HSIC against multiple clinical outcomes, capturing nonlinear risk relationships beyond traditional Charlson/Elixhauser scores. Backed by theory characterizing when unified orderings exist.

entry.title: FllumaOne: A Code-Native Multimodal CAD Dataset with Executable Programs and Kernel-Validated Feature Histories

author.name: Jizong Zhan

entry.summary: Introduces FllumaOne, a code-native multimodal CAD dataset of 100K models generated by executable Python programs with kernel-validated feature histories, geometry, point clouds, descriptions, and renderings. Supports editable CAD research by exposing modeling operations and feature dependencies.

entry.title: WallZero: Mastering the Game of WallGo with Strategic Analysis

author.name: Hsing-Yu Chen, J\'er\^ome Arjonilla, I-Chen Wu, Ti-Rong Wu

entry.summary: Introduces DecoSearch, a training-free text-to-SQL framework that routes queries by complexity, escalating complex ones to a DAG of atomic sub-questions with plan-level repair and RAG grounding. Schema pruning and an LLM judger allocate reasoning effort appropriately.

entry.title: StepGuard: Guarding Web Navigation via Single-Step Calibration

author.name: Zhihao Cui, Yuchen Zhang, Xiyang Sun, Yaxiong Wang, Li Zhu, Jinpeng Hu, Liu Liu, Mengjia Li, Yujiao Wu

entry.summary: Proposes StepGuard for web navigation, combining Dynamic Dual-Policy Optimization to mitigate reward conflict between navigation and answering, and Confidence-Guided Adaptive Navigation Reflection to calibrate single-step errors. Targets reward misalignment and error propagation in VLM-RL web agents.

entry.title: IsabeLLM: Automated Theorem Proving Applied to Formally Verifying Consensus

author.name: Elliot Jones, William Knottenbelt

entry.summary: Presents IsabeLLM, applying AI-driven automated theorem proving to formally verify blockchain consensus protocols, aiming to make formal verification more accessible by automating expert workload. Motivated by frequent costly exploits in blockchain systems.

entry.title: Your AI Travel Agent Would Book You a Bullfight: An Agentic Benchmark for Implicit Animal Welfare in Frontier AI Models

author.name: Jasmine Brazilek, Oliver Tulio, Joel Christoph, Miles Tidmarsh, Carol Kline, Arturs Kanepajs

entry.summary: Tests frontier AI on ten research-level math problems (note: this entry duplicates the First Proof Second Batch concept); the actual paper is the WallZero AlphaZero agent for the board game WallGo, introducing tailored action and feature designs that defeat professional Go players and analyze game fairness.

entry.title: Towards Distributed Inference of LLMs on a P2P Network

author.name: Shabari S Nair, Krishanu Saini

entry.summary: Proposes a decentralized, prefix-cache-aware routing scheme for peer-to-peer LLM serving where each node maintains a radix tree of cached prefixes and gossips estimates of peers, routing to the longest estimated prefix match. Stale metadata only causes cache misses, making weak consistency sufficient for correctness.

entry.title: KFTD: Koopman-Fourier Time-Differentiable Network for Continuous Ocean Spatiotemporal Forecasting

author.name: Qinghui Chen, Zekai Zhang, Hailong Liu, Jinglin Zhang, Cong Bai

entry.summary: Presents KFTD, a Koopman-Fourier time-differentiable network for continuous ocean spatiotemporal forecasting that maps nonlinear dynamics into Koopman linear space and uses Fourier analysis for continuous-time interpolation at arbitrary sub-steps. Decouples interpolation from prediction for efficiency without diffusion models.

entry.title: MIVE: A Minimalist Integer Vector Engine for Softmax LayerNorm and RMSNorm Acceleration

author.name: Kosmas Alexandridis, Giorgos Dimitrakopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes a minimalist integer vector engine that executes Softmax, LayerNorm, and RMSNorm within a unified datapath, avoiding the duplicated hardware blocks typical of LLM accelerators. Targets reduced silicon utilization for inference.

entry.title: Accelerated Convex Optimization via Hamiltonian Dynamics with Deterministic Integration Time

author.name: Xiuyuan Wang, Vishwak Srinivasan, Qiang Fu, Siddharth Mitra, Ashia Wilson, Andre Wibisono

entry.summary: This paper develops Hamiltonian dynamics-based optimization algorithms achieving accelerated convergence for smooth convex objectives by exploiting contraction of averaged flow trajectories. It extends prior work limited to quadratics or expectation-only guarantees.

entry.title: On the Memorization Behavior of LLMs in Generative Recommendation: Observations, Implications, and Training Strategies

author.name: Sunwoo Kim, Sunkyung Lee, Clark Mingxuan Ju, Donald Loveland, Bhuvesh Kumar, Kijung Shin, Neil Shah, Liam Collins

entry.summary: This work examines LLM memorization behavior in generative recommendation, showing LLMs perform one-hop memorization more than non-LLM baselines, which restricts their use of pretrained knowledge. It proposes training strategies to mitigate this and improve generalization.

entry.title: Bounded Difference Concentration for Infinitely Exchangeable Sequences with Applications to AI Benchmark Uncertainty

author.name: Fangyuan Lin, Spencer Frei, Victor H. de la Pena

entry.summary: This paper derives bounded-difference concentration inequalities for functions of infinitely exchangeable sequences by conditioning on the de Finetti directing measure. It applies these to AI benchmark uncertainty, showing the latent mixture term cancels for zero-sum linear contrasts.

entry.title: Tensor-based second-order causal discovery

author.name: Nathan Ouyang, Kexin Wan, Anna Seigal

entry.summary: Introduces a tensor-based algorithm for causal discovery that uses second-order statistics from observational and interventional covariance matrices to recover a DAG and edge functions under linear SEMs. Focusing on second-order moments offers statistical and computational efficiency over higher-moment approaches.

entry.title: Multi-Source Cybersecurity Logs: An ATT&CK-Labeled Dataset and SLM Evaluation

author.name: Abir Ashab Niloy, Ahmed Ryan, Imamul Hossain Rafi, Md Erfan, Md Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: Builds the first public multi-source cybersecurity log dataset (system, network, browser) with per-entry MITRE ATT&CK technique labels and evaluates small language models on detecting multi-stage attacks. It fills a gap left by single-source or coarsely-labeled datasets.

entry.title: A Practical Evaluation Method for Long-Form Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Yulin Xue, Siqi Ouyang, Lei Li

entry.summary: Presents a reproducible evaluation method for long-form simultaneous speech-to-speech translation using ASR, forced alignment, and embedding-based sentence aligners to recover timestamps and compute sentence-level quality and latency. It addresses the lack of practical evaluation for continuous end-to-end SimulS2ST systems.

entry.title: Evaluating and Preserving Lexical Stress in English-to-Chinese Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Yuchen Song, Xi Chen, Mingze Li, Satoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: Investigates English-to-Chinese speech-to-speech translation of lexical stress, building a stress-annotated Chinese dataset, an XLS-R-based Mandarin stress detector, and a novel cross-lingual stress evaluation metric, then fine-tuning CosyVoice3 for stress-aware translation. It addresses underexplored prosodic emphasis transfer for tonal languages.

entry.title: Beyond NL2Code: A Structured Survey of Multimodal Code Intelligence

author.name: Xuanle Zhao, Qiushi Sun, Jingyu Xiao, Xuexin Liu, Haoyue Yang, Qiaosheng Chen, Xianzhen Luo, Jing Huang, Yufeng Zhong, Lei Chen, Shuai Fu, Zhenlin Wei, Jinhe Bi, Lei Jiang, Haibo Qiu, Siqi Yang, Peng Shi, Jian Hu, Zhixiong Zeng

entry.summary: A structured survey of multimodal code intelligence, covering systems that generate, edit, or reason with code from visually grounded inputs like screenshots, charts, and UI states. It organizes the field by the role code plays in each task, offering a useful taxonomy for an emerging research area.

entry.title: From Awareness to Adherence: Bridging the Context Gap in Spoken Dialogue Systems via Context-Aware Decoding

author.name: Che Hyun Lee, Heeseung Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: This work identifies a gap in spoken dialogue systems between latent context awareness and active adherence, where models recognize relevant history internally but parametric priors override it during decoding. It proposes audio-adapted Context-Aware Decoding that contrasts output distributions with and without key historical context.

entry.title: Sycophancy as Material Failure under Pushback Loading: A Multi-Axis Characterization Across Three Loading Cases and up to Seventeen Material Charges

author.name: Ferdinand M. Schessl

entry.summary: This paper applies a materials-science framing to sycophancy, treating conversation as a test specimen under progressive pushback load and stance-flips as material failure, characterized across three loading cases and up to 17 model charges with 7,800 specimens. It offers a multi-axis quantitative characterization addressing low construct agreement on sycophancy.

entry.title: Connecting Speech to Words through Images

author.name: Gabriel Pirlogeanu, Dan Oneata, Horia Cucu, Herman Kamper

entry.summary: This work presents a visually grounded method for building a spoken word vocabulary using only images and their spoken descriptions, without text supervision. It uses image captioning to derive written words, finds utterances whose captions contain them, and applies unsupervised word discovery to align spoken instances.

entry.title: Contrastive-Difference CKA Reveals Concept-Specific Structural Alignment Across Language Model Architectures

author.name: Xueping Gao

entry.summary: This work introduces contrastive-difference CKA, a training-free diagnostic computing kernel alignment on per-sample contrastive differences, to characterize a geometric-functional universality dissociation across LLM architectures. It finds moderate geometric convergence coexisting with near-perfect functional transfer across concept domains.

entry.title: Exploring Extrinsic and Intrinsic Properties for Effective Reasoning with Code Interpreter

author.name: Patomporn Payoungkhamdee, Napat Laosaengpha, Jenta Wonglertsakul, Pittawat Taveekitworachai, Pume Tuchinda, Panjapong Poobanchuen, Ekapol Chuangsuwanich, Can Udomcharoenchaikit, Samuel Cahyawijaya, Peerat Limkonchotiwat, Sarana Nutanong

entry.summary: This work investigates effective reasoning with a code interpreter from extrinsic (crucial tokens) and intrinsic (code-specific cognitive behaviors) perspectives, finding stronger code-reasoning models exhibit higher prevalence of both. It analyzes the behavioral properties underlying effective executable reasoning across multiple LLMs.

entry.title: When the Same Musical Knowledge Forgets Differently: A Clean Probe of Pathway-Dependent Forgetting

author.name: Yu Liu, Zhiwei Yang, Wenxiao Zhang, Cong Cao, Fangfang Yuan, Kun Peng, Haimei Qin, Lei Jiang, Jin B. Hong, Hao Peng, Yanbing Liu

entry.summary: This paper tests the Pathway-Invariant Assumption, asking whether the modality through which multimodal models acquire knowledge (audio vs text) affects how easily that knowledge is later forgotten, using music understanding as a clean controlled probe. It finds acquisition route does influence forgetting. An interesting conceptual contribution to multimodal forgetting research.

entry.title: PreLort: Prefix-Nested LoRA for Federated Fine-Tuning under Rank Heterogeneity

author.name: Muhammad Waseem, Nurbek Tastan, Andrej Jovanovic, Nicholas D. Lane, Nils Lukas, Karthik Nandakumar, Samuel Horvath

entry.summary: PreLort introduces a nested low-rank LoRA formulation for federated fine-tuning under client rank heterogeneity, organizing adapter dimensions into a prefix hierarchy so lower ranks encode task-relevant information and higher ranks capture extra detail. It addresses aggregation challenges across heterogeneous hardware. Useful for privacy-preserving federated LLM adaptation.

entry.title: Know Your Limits : On the Faithfulness of LLMs as Solvers and Autoformalizers in Legal Reasoning

author.name: Olivia Peiyu Wang, Sanna Wong-Toropainen, Daneshvar Amrollahi, Ryan Bai, Tashvi Bansal, Arush Garg, Leilani H. Gilpin

entry.summary: This study examines whether LLM legal reasoning reflects faithful logical inference or heuristic approximation by comparing pure LLM classification, LLM-based formal reasoning, and Z3 SMT solver-based reasoning on a re-annotated ContractNLI subset. It reveals a measurable gap between pragmatic legal interpretation and strict formal entailment. Relevant for trustworthy legal AI.

entry.title: DoubtProbe: Black-Box Jailbreak Defense via Structural Verification and Semantic Auditing

author.name: Xuanyu Yin, Yilin Jiang, Jun Zhou, Kai Chen, Zhengfu Cao, Xiaolei Dong

entry.summary: DoubtProbe is a dual-branch inference-time black-box jailbreak defense combining structural verification with semantic auditing, motivated by the observation that many jailbreaks reorganize rather than remove the harmful goal, leaving it recoverable during generation. It avoids reliance on known-attack coverage. Relevant for practical LLM safety.

entry.title: OpenClaw-Skill: Collective Skill Tree Search for Agentic Large Language Models

author.name: Tianyi Lin, Chuanyu Sun, Jingyi Zhang, Changxu Wei, Huanjin Yao, Shunyu Liu, Xikun Zhang, Liu Liu, Jiaxing Huang

entry.summary: OpenClaw-Skill introduces Collective Skill Tree Search, a tree-search-based framework that automatically constructs structured, diverse, generalizable reusable skills for LLM agents through collective skill node generation and assessment phases. It enhances tool use, multi-step reasoning, and dynamic environment interaction. Relevant to agentic skill learning.

entry.title: GeneralVLA-2: Geometry-Aware Reconstruction and Governed Memory for Robot Planning

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Guoqing Ma, Zeyu Zhang, Yandong Guo, Boxin Shi, Hao Tang

entry.summary: GeneralVLA-2 improves generalist vision-language-action robot planning with geometry-aware reconstruction to reduce monocular hallucination of pose and unseen geometry using calibrated multi-view observations, plus a governed memory that controls quality, conflicts, confidence, and geometric relevance rather than naively appending knowledge. It addresses two bottlenecks in hierarchical RGB-D to trajectory planning. Relevant for robot manipulation.

entry.title: ActWorld: From Explorable to Interactive World Model via Action-Aware Memory

author.name: Zhexiao Xiong, Yizhi Song, Hao Kang, Qing Yan, Liming Jiang, Jenson Yang, Zhoujie Fu, Stathi Fotiadis, Angtian Wang, Zichuan Liu, Bo Liu, Yiding Yang, Xin Lu, Nathan Jacobs

entry.summary: ActWorld extends interactive world models from navigation-only to mid-rollout object interaction via action-aware memory in a chunk-autoregressive framework. It addresses the gap where prior world models are explorable but not truly actionable.

entry.title: Energy-efficient codon optimization on thermodynamic hardware

author.name: Andraz Jelincic, Ross C. Walker

entry.summary: This paper maps mRNA codon optimization to an Ising-model sampling problem executable on thermodynamic hardware, presenting what the authors call the first concrete pharmaceutical application with energy estimates grounded in prototype measurements. It promises orders-of-magnitude energy savings for combinatorial drug-development tasks.

entry.title: WAM-RL: World-Action Model Reinforcement Learning with Reconstruction Rewards and Online Video SFT

author.name: Zezhong Qian, Xiaowei Chi, Yu Qi, Haozhan Li, Zhi Yang Chen, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: WAM-RL is a reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes a world model and action model through online environment interaction, using reconstruction rewards and online video supervised fine-tuning to go beyond expert-trajectory imitation. It enables fine-grained manipulation skills and continuous improvement.

entry.title: ThinkingVLA: Interleaved Vision and Language Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Tianyi Lu, Hui Zhang, Zijie Diao, Junke Wang, Shengqi Xu, Xingyao Lin, Guojin Zhong, Ziyi Ye, Peng Wang, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: ThinkingVLA proposes an interleaved vision-and-language reasoning architecture for robotic manipulation, decomposing planning into forward prediction of the next visual state and inverse dynamics inference of actions within a unified autoregressive model. It adds explicit inverse reasoning lacking in prior CoT-based VLA methods.

entry.title: How the AI Village works

author.name: Adam B

entry.summary: Announces that over a year of multi-agent trajectory data from the AI Village—where AI agents pursue long-horizon goals collaboratively using computers—is now available on HuggingFace. Explains the setup, schedule, and how the agents operate.

entry.title: Surrogate Assisted Pedestrian Protection Design via a Foundation Model Orchestrated Workflow

author.name: Osamu Ito, Akihiko Katagiri, Yoshikazu Nakagawa, Shin Saeki, Jun Shiraishi, Masato Sasaki

entry.summary: Presents the first foundation-model-orchestrated workflow for crash-safety pedestrian protection design, using surrogate models to cut CAE simulation evaluation from hours to seconds while predicting leg injury metrics at R-squared 0.87. Tackles highly nonlinear crash dynamics with data-driven surrogates.

entry.title: FlowRAG: Synergizing Explicit Reasoning via Frequency-Aware Multi-Granularity Graph Flow

author.name: Bihao Zhan, Zongsheng Cao, Jie Zhou, Bo Zhang, Liang He

entry.summary: Proposes FlowRAG, a graph-based RAG framework constructing a quad-level heterogeneous graph with frequency-aware multi-granularity flow to improve semantic recall and explicit multi-hop reasoning. Addresses under-retrieval for abstract queries and brittle entity-to-entity transitions.

entry.title: MathVis-Fine: Aligning Visual Supervision with Necessity via Progressive Dependency-Guided Training for Multimodal Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Wanshi Xu, Haokun Zhao, Haidong Yuan, Songjun Cao, Long Ma

entry.summary: Proposes MathVis-Fine, aligning visual supervision with its actual necessity via progressive dependency-guided training for multimodal mathematical reasoning. Addresses coarse, uniform visual reward signals that ignore sample-specific text-image dependencies.

entry.title: Learning to Refine Hidden States for Reliable LLM Reasoning

author.name: Chia-Hsuan Hsu, Jui-Ming Yao

entry.summary: ReLAR is a reinforcement-guided framework that iteratively refines LLM hidden states before decoding to stabilize multi-step reasoning. It uses learned controllers to adaptively determine refinement depth and direction without explicit chain-of-thought generation.

entry.title: From Drift to Coherence: Stabilizing Beliefs in LLMs

author.name: SongEun Kim, Seungyoo Lee, Edwin Fong, Hyungi Lee, Juho Lee

entry.summary: This work studies whether LLMs satisfy the martingale property of predictive beliefs in multiple-choice QA, finding early-stage belief drift but eventual stabilization after sufficient resampling. It introduces prompted predictive resampling to probe belief coherence.

entry.title: AoiZora: Topology-Aware Auto-Parallel Optimization for Inference of Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Kaijian Wang, Yuanyuan Xu, Fanjiang Ye, Ye Cao, Jingwei Zuo, T. S. Eugene Ng, Yarong Mu, Yuke Wang

entry.summary: AoiZora is a compiler-mediated topology-aware auto-parallel planner for distributed inference of diffusion transformers, optimizing how sharding is laid out on physical TPU interconnects. It addresses the oversight in current auto-parallel systems that ignore physical layout.

entry.title: Finite-Time Queue Peak Laws in Stochastic Networks: Logarithmic Scaling After Geometric Thresholds

author.name: Hao Liang, Cheng Tang, Yunzong Xu

entry.summary: Proves finite-horizon queue-peak scaling laws for generalized switches under uniform slack, showing the square-root envelope persists only up to a geometric threshold beyond which the running maximum grows only logarithmically. This sharpens understanding of MaxWeight-style scheduling behavior.

entry.title: PACUTE: Phonology-, Affix-, and Character-level Understanding of Tokens for Filipino

author.name: Jann Railey Montalan, David Demitri Africa, Jimson Paulo Layacan, Richell Isaiah Flores, Ivan Yuri De Leon, Lance Calvin Gamboa

entry.summary: Introduces PACUTE, a 4,600-task diagnostic benchmark evaluating phonological, affixal, and character-level morphological understanding of Filipino in LLMs, targeting non-concatenative morphology like infixation and reduplication. It pinpoints where subword tokenizers misalign with morpheme boundaries.

entry.title: Can LLM Coding Agents Reason About Time Series?

author.name: Filip Rechtor\'ik, Ond\v{r}ej Du\v{s}ek, Zden\v{e}k Kasner

entry.summary: This study examines whether LLM coding agents can reason about time series, comparing raw numerical input, LLM-as-coding-agent, and combinations across two benchmarks. Agents with code access outperform raw-data processing by up to 10%, but still answer 22-34% of questions incorrectly.

entry.title: Revisiting the Systematicity in Negation in the Era of In-Context Learning

author.name: Hitomi Yanaka, Taisei Yamamoto

entry.summary: This work analyzes systematicity in negation understanding under in-context learning from both behavioral and representational perspectives, finding LLMs partially recognize negation scope but fail to achieve perfect performance, with difficulty varying by output format. It also examines whether robust function vectors can be constructed for negation.

entry.title: Multimodal Evaluator Preference Collapse: Cross-Modal Contagion in Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: This paper shows Evaluator Preference Collapse is dramatically amplified in multimodal self-evolving agents, with one strategy absorbing 48.4% of weight (3.2x text-only collapse), and introduces cross-modal contagion where preferences acquired in one modality corrupt strategy selection in another. It uses a four-phase isolation paradigm to measure contagion coefficients. Important caution for self-evolving multimodal agents.

entry.title: Scaling LLM Reasoning from Minimal Labels: A Semi-Supervised Framework with a Lightweight Verifier

author.name: Keizo Kato, Chenhui Chu, Yugo Murawaki, Sado Kurohashi

entry.summary: This semi-supervised framework scales LLM reasoning from minimal labels by training a lightweight reasoning-correctness classifier on a few labeled samples to judge intermediate traces, then filtering with an entropy-based confidence threshold to fine-tune on high-confidence pseudo-reasoning. It turns verification into a data creation mechanism. Useful for reducing annotation cost in reasoning training.

entry.title: SPHINX: First Explain, Then Explore

author.name: Nguyen Do, Tue M. Cao, Tien Van Do, Andr\'as Hajdu, Tam\'as B\'erczes, My T. Thai

entry.summary: SPHINX is a closed-loop framework for adversarial driving scenario synthesis guided by the principle of first explaining the driving policy's failure diagnosis (e.g., indecisiveness, multi-frame inconsistency) then exploring scenarios targeting those weaknesses, rather than relying on LLM prior assumptions. It targets evaluation and improvement of autonomous vehicle decision-making. Relevant for AV safety testing.

entry.title: TaFD: Threat-Aware Frequency Decoupling for Adversarial Robustness against Heterogeneous Attacks

author.name: Mengda Xie, Yiling He, Meie Fang

entry.summary: TaFD is a two-stage threat-aware frequency-decoupling defense that addresses negative transfer in joint adversarial training between Lp-bounded and semantic attacks, formalizing gradient incompatibility via first-order analysis and exploiting separable spectral characteristics to apply a frequency-domain divide-and-conquer strategy. It improves multi-threat robustness. Relevant to adversarial robustness research.

entry.title: Predicting Immune Biomarkers with MultiModal Mixture-of-Expert Pathology Foundation Models Empowers Precision Oncology

author.name: Tianyu Liu, Ziqing Wang, Zhaokang Liang, Tong Ding, Peter Humphrey, Lorraine Col\'on-Cartagena, Emily Ling-Lin Pai, Kenneth Tou En Chang, Mohamed Kahila, Jonathan Chong Kai Liew, Tinglin Huang, Rex Ying, Kaize Ding, Faisal Mahmood, Wengong Jin

entry.summary: MixTIME is a multimodal mixture-of-experts pathology foundation model that integrates image-only, image-text, and image-transcriptomic experts to predict immune biomarkers from H&E whole-slide images. It targets precision oncology by estimating multiplex immunofluorescence protein expression.

entry.title: A Polyak-Ruppert Central Limit Theorem for SA-Adam with Momentum and Non-Convergent Adaptive Preconditioning

author.name: Sunyoung An, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: This paper proves a non-autonomous Polyak-Ruppert central limit theorem for SA-Adam with momentum and non-convergent adaptive preconditioning, treating the augmented (iterate, momentum) state as a time-varying linear stochastic approximation. It establishes when averaged adaptive optimizers yield valid one-pass statistical inference.

entry.title: MapSatisfyBench: Benchmarking Satisfaction-Aware Map Agents through Behavior-Grounded Implicit Decision Factors

author.name: Lubin Bai, Mengyu Cao, Sixue Wang, Zhongwei Wan, Yue Pan, Jiale Hou, Xiang Li, Xiuyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MapSatisfyBench, a benchmark for evaluating whether map-service LLM agents can proactively recover implicit, unspoken user decision factors from available information. Addresses underspecified everyday queries that require satisfaction-aware reasoning.

entry.title: FinAcumen: Financial Multimodal Reasoning via Self-Evolving Experience Memory Harness

author.name: Pianran Guo, Pengcheng Zhou, Yucheng Jian, Shuhua Chen

entry.summary: Presents FinAcumen, a financial multimodal reasoning agent with selective experience memory that accumulates grounded reasoning experience across episodes to improve tool routing and reduce hallucination. Coordinates numerical, retrieval, visual, and temporal reasoning over heterogeneous evidence.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Context-Aware and Relation-Aware Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Haoyang Zhong, Yifei Sun, Antong Zhang, Chunping Wang, Lei Chen, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes HyGRAG, a hierarchical graph RAG framework that genuinely fuses contextual and relational knowledge rather than retrieving entity-centric and chunk-centric representations separately. Aims to produce summaries that integrate context and relations for emergent understanding.

entry.title: Software Delegation Contracts: Measuring Reviewability in AI Coding-Agent Work

author.name: Vincent Schmalbach

entry.summary: Reports a controlled pilot study measuring the effects of explicit software delegation contracts for AI coding agents, comparing realistic issue prompts versus explicit contracts across 64 executions on a seeded-defect TypeScript task environment. Examines reviewability of delegated coding work under bounded authority.

entry.title: Dimensionality Controls When Modularity Helps in Continual Learning

author.name: Kathrin Korte, Christian Medeiros Adriano, Joachim Winther Pedersen, Eleni Nisioti, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: Investigates how modular architecture, task similarity, and representational dimensionality jointly shape compositional continual learning in an A-B-A paradigm. Finds that explicit modularity helps little in high-dimensional lazy regimes but matters in low-dimensional ones.

entry.title: MGUP: A Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy for Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Da Chang, Ganzhao Yuan

entry.summary: MGUP is a momentum-gradient alignment update policy that applies larger step-sizes to a selected proportion of parameters while keeping smaller steps for others, integrating with AdamW, Lion, and Muon. It offers fine-grained selective updates with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Sign-Rank, Index, and List Replicability: Connections and Separations

author.name: Ari Blondal, Hamed Hatami, Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov, Sivan Tretiak

entry.summary: This paper establishes connections and separations between sign rank, the Z2-index, and list replicability in learning theory. It resolves an open question by showing a strong separation between sign rank and Z2-index.

entry.title: Turning music identification into a neural forward pass

author.name: Muhammad Taimoor Haseeb, Ahmad Hammoudeh, Gus Xia

entry.summary: This work turns music identification from a System-2 rule-based search pipeline into a single neural feed-forward pass by a generative transformer that predicts track identifiers directly from audio excerpts. It mimics associative human recognition rather than explicit candidate enumeration.

entry.title: Damage Adaptation in Seconds for Architected Materials

author.name: James Avtges, Jake Ketchum, Helena Young, Taekyoung Kim, Ryan Truby, Todd Murphey

entry.summary: This work enables proprioceptive adaptation to catastrophic damage in soft-actuated architected materials in under one minute, using latent damage representations and a simple ensemble method. It identifies conditions where exponential sample complexity collapses to linear.

entry.title: Differential Privacy of Gaussian Process Posterior Sampling

author.name: Tomasz Maciazek

entry.summary: This work studies the differential privacy of releasing Gaussian process posterior sample paths, showing the intrinsic randomness of posterior sampling yields Renyi-DP guarantees without external noise. It separates posterior-mean leakage from covariance leakage and validates with membership inference attacks.

entry.title: Let LLMs Judge Each Other: Multi-Agent Peer-Reviewed Reasoning for Medical Question Answering

author.name: Zaifu Zhan, Shuang Zhou, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent peer-reviewed reasoning method where multiple LLM agents generate chain-of-thought answers then review each other's reasoning for factual correctness and logic, selecting the highest-rated chain. It improves accuracy and interpretability on medical QA benchmarks over single-model CoT.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Stance Detection in Scientific Discourse: A Test Case in Bayesian Cognitive Science

author.name: Eyup Engin Kucuk, Tarik Kelestemur, \"Omer Da\u{g}lar Tanrikulu

entry.summary: Studies LLM-assisted stance detection in scientific discourse, using a theory-driven codebook and diagnostic-gated prompt optimization to classify whether authors treat Bayesian cognitive models as realist or instrumentalist across three frontier LLMs. It validates LLMs for interpretive qualitative coding with multi-rater reliability analysis.

entry.title: Distilling Examples into Task Instructions: Enhanced In-Context Learning for Real-World B2B Conversations

author.name: Guy Rotman, Adi Kopilov, Danit Berger Zalmanson, Omri Allouche

entry.summary: Introduces the Call Playbook dataset of five classification tasks from real B2B sales conversations and proposes knowledge-extraction methods that distill verbose few-shot examples into compact interpretable task instructions for in-context learning. It addresses ICL limitations as context length grows with concatenated examples.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Multi-Dimensional Empirical Study of LLMs for Conversation Summarization

author.name: Weixiao Zhou, Gengyao Li, Xianfu Cheng, Junnan Zhu, Feifei Zhai, Zhoujun Li

entry.summary: OmniCSEval is a large-scale benchmark for conversation summarization spanning 1,800 conversations across six scenarios with context lengths up to 32k tokens, using a bidirectional fact-checking framework to assess completeness, conciseness, and faithfulness. It includes frontier reasoning systems and small models.

entry.title: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection

author.name: Y. H. Zhou, Z. M. Ma, Y. J. Zhou, Y. T. Li, H. X. Xiang, Y. M. Cheng, T. L. Chen, K. J. Zhang, Z. H. Nan, J. H. Ni, Z. Wu, Q. Y. Pan, S. Zhang, S. Cheng, M. Y. Luo

entry.summary: FraudSMSWalker is a controlled benchmark for URL-masked SMS-to-webpage fraud detection requiring models to judge how SMS claims align with sanitized webpage content and requested actions, avoiding reputation shortcuts. It contains 699 bilingual chains across ten service scenarios.

entry.title: The Art of Mixology: Mixup-based Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving Split Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Chen, Xiang Gao, Xianshun Wang, Chengran Li, Shengyu Xia, Xueluan Gong, Linru Zhang, Qian Wang, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: MIXGUARD is a mixup-based privacy-preserving split learning framework for LLMs introducing token-level obfuscation to defend against data reconstruction attacks while balancing utility, efficiency, and stability. It targets the difficult tradeoff among these factors in resource-constrained split training.

entry.title: MAGE-RAG: Multigranular Adaptive Graph Evidence for Agentic Multimodal RAG in Long-Document QA

author.name: Yilong Zuo, Xunkai Li, Jing Yuan, Qiangqiang Dai, Hongchao Qin, Ronghua Li

entry.summary: MAGE-RAG is a multigranular adaptive graph evidence framework for long-document multimodal QA that uses page retrieval as an entry point and builds query-time graph evidence to balance coverage, noise, and inference cost across text, tables, images, and charts. It improves on fixed top-k retrieval. Relevant for multimodal RAG.

entry.title: SierpinskiCam: Camera-Controlled Video Retaking with Sierpinski Triangle Pattern Cues

author.name: Suttisak Wizadwongsa, Hyelin Nam, Supasorn Suwajanakorn, Jeong Joon Park

entry.summary: SierpinskiCam tackles single-video camera-controlled video retaking by augmenting geometry-based guidance with Sierpinski dome texture cues that provide rich trackable features even under large viewpoint changes, addressing the degradation of geometry guidance when the target camera departs from the source trajectory. It improves rendering of newly revealed regions. A creative video diffusion guidance technique.

entry.title: StereoFactory: A Unified Merging Framework for Robust Stereo Matching

author.name: Xianda Guo, Pinhan Fu, Ruilin Wang, Wenke Huang, Mang Ye, Qin Zou

entry.summary: StereoFactory is a coarse-to-fine evolutionary framework for adaptive model merging in stereo matching, using a genetic algorithm to search which specialized models should participate then resolving module-level interference, offering a scalable post-hoc alternative to costly joint retraining. It addresses harmful task-vector interference in existing merging methods. Relevant for scalable stereo foundation models.

entry.title: Universal Image Restoration via Internalized Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yu Guo, Zhengru Fang, Shengfeng He, Senkang Hu, Yihang Tao, Phone Lin, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: CoTIR is a universal image restoration framework that internalizes chain-of-thought reasoning within a single model by viewing restoration as a specialized subtask of image editing, avoiding the high computational cost and weak degradation-interaction modeling of multi-round CoT with specialized modules. It targets complex mixed degradations. Relevant for all-in-one restoration.

entry.title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports

author.name: Samar Ansari

entry.summary: This single-author study measures information degradation when LLMs rewrite radiology reports, quantifying entity erosion, hedging collapse (loss of clinical uncertainty), and cross-modal alignment changes across three rewriting tasks. It finds a dissociation between information loss and cross-modal fidelity.

entry.title: DexLink Hand: A Compact, Affordable, 16-DOF Linkage-Driven Hand with Human-Like Dexterity

author.name: Hao Wu, Yanzhe Wang, Yu Feng, Jian Liu, Jihao Li, Jianshu Zhou, Huixu Dong

entry.summary: DexLink Hand is a compact, low-cost (under USD 400, 320g) 16-actuator, 20-joint linkage-driven anthropomorphic hand achieving human-like dexterity within a human-sized form. It addresses the dexterity-compactness-affordability trade-off in robotic hands.

entry.title: LLM-as-Judge in Education: A Curriculum-Grounded Marking Pipeline

author.name: Xiwei Xu, Chen Wang, Jacky Jiang, Phil Yang, Qian Fu, Mohan Dhall, Wenjie Zhang, Liming Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a curriculum-grounded LLM-as-Judge pipeline for question-level exam marking that grounds outputs in authorized curriculum artifacts and marking guidelines, co-developed with an industry partner. Targets high-stakes exam preparation for university admission.

entry.title: Memory as a Wasting Asset: Pricing Flash Endurance for Embodied Agents, and the Limits of Doing So

author.name: Josef Liyanjun Chen

entry.summary: Treats embodied-agent flash memory as depreciating non-renewable capital, pricing write endurance with a single shadow price to make cost-optimal memory placement across RAM/NVM/cloud a threshold rule. Measures the value-write association on real robot logs and identifies limits of the approach.

entry.title: ParkingTransformer: LLM-Enhanced End-to-End Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Parking

author.name: Hauteng Wu, Xu Li, Dong Kong, Zihang Wang, Xieyuanli Chen, Benwu Wang, Wenkai Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes ParkingTransformer, an end-to-end autonomous parking trajectory planner that combines multi-view perception with LLM scene-understanding, interacting directly with historical and raw sensor data to output trajectories without dense bird's-eye-view representations. Adds interpretability and semantic understanding to black-box parking.

entry.title: Amortized Probabilistic Retrieval of Atmospheric CO2 from OCO-2 Spectra Using Deep Learning with Laplace Approximations and Normalizing Flows

author.name: Alejandro Calle-Saldarriaga, Felix Jimenez, Jack Grosskreuz, Jiazheng Wang, Jonathan Hobbs, Matthias Katzfuss

entry.summary: A deep learning framework for retrieving atmospheric CO2 from satellite spectra using Laplace approximations and normalizing flows for uncertainty quantification. It offers a faster alternative to expensive operational retrieval algorithms validated on high-fidelity simulations.

entry.title: When the Next Step Is Not One Step: Distribution-Aware Execution Modeling for Concurrent Go Programs

author.name: Kaviru Hapuarachchi

entry.summary: This work uses scheduler nondeterminism in concurrent Go programs as a training signal, fine-tuning a 7B model to match empirical distributions of next-events via KL objective. It improves prediction accuracy on real production bugs from CockroachDB, Kubernetes, and others.

entry.title: An expressivity analysis of hierarchical modelling in deep transformers via bounded-depth grammars

author.name: Vinoth Nandakumar, Qiang Qu, Pramod Thebe, Sakshi Khachariya, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This work analyzes the expressiveness of deep transformers in representing hierarchical structures through the lens of bounded-depth, non-recursive context-free grammars. It provides rigorous theory for how depth enables hierarchical representations in language modeling.

entry.title: Fast Nonparametric Conditional Independence Testing via Two-Stage Regression

author.name: Eric V. Strobl

entry.summary: BLITZ is a fast nonparametric conditional independence test designed for constraint-based causal discovery, running under a second while maintaining calibration. It uses two-stage residualization combining low-order polynomial regression with shallow tree regressions.

entry.title: Evaluating Open-Source LLMs for Multi-Label ATT&CK Technique Classification on CTI Reports

author.name: Ahmed Ryan, Saad Sakib Noor, Md Erfan, Shaswata Mitra, Sudip Mittal, Md Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: Evaluates open-source LLMs on multi-label MITRE ATT&CK technique classification from realistic unstructured cyber threat intelligence reports, showing prior single-technique evaluations inflate performance. It establishes more honest baselines for complex, multi-step attack pattern recognition.

entry.title: CoCoGEC: Counterfactual Generation for Robust Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Qianyu Wang, Xiaoman Wang, Yuanyuan Liang, Xinyuan Li, Yunshi Lan

entry.summary: Proposes CoCoGEC, a counterfactual generation framework for grammatical error correction that alters error-irrelevant context to improve robustness against context perturbations and label-flipping. It targets GEC models' tendency to fail when surrounding context shifts.

entry.title: DYNA : Dynamic Episodic Memory Networks for Augmenting Large Language Models with Temporal Knowledge Graphs in Continuous Learning

author.name: Ali Sarabadani, Mahtab Tajvidiyan

entry.summary: Proposes DYNA, a lightweight framework augmenting a frozen LLM with a temporal knowledge graph as updatable external memory, retrieving relevant nodes via random walks and centrality, reducing catastrophic forgetting by ~7% versus fine-tuning and improving temporal ordering ~5% over standard RAG. It links graph clustering structure to retrieval quality.

entry.title: Interactor: Agentic RL oriented Iterative Creation for Ad Description Generation in Sponsored Search

author.name: Penghui Wei, Jiayu Wu, Chao Ye, Zhi Guo, Shuanglong Li, Lin Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Interactor, a multi-turn iterative creation framework optimized with agentic RL for generating informative ad descriptions in sponsored search, where the generation policy interacts with an environment of multiple generative reward models evaluating knowledge capacity and selling points. It targets longer-span descriptions that incorporate world knowledge to address search intent.

entry.title: FinBalance: A Multi-Document Accounting Reconciliation Benchmark

author.name: Sasank Tumpati, Devansh Agarwal, Ayush Kedia, Arjun Neekhra, Murari Mandal, Krishna Garg, Yash Sinha, Suman Gupta, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: FinBalance is a multi-document accounting reconciliation benchmark built from synthetic source-document bundles across industries and difficulty levels, requiring models to produce journal entries, balance sheets, and detect inconsistencies. It targets realistic earlier-stage accounting workflows rather than prepared financial artifacts.

entry.title: In-Domain Supervised Pathology Report Classification: A Reproducible Pipeline from Data Curation to Production-Matched Evaluation

author.name: Isaac Hands, Bin Huang, Adam Spannaus, John Gounley, Heidi Hanson, Eric Durbin, Sally R. Ellingson

entry.summary: This paper presents a reproducible in-domain supervised pipeline for pathology report classification that counters out-of-distribution performance drops across cancer registries, emphasizing low false-negative rates and manageable reviewer workload. It standardizes data curation with facility-stratified sampling and production-matched holdouts.

entry.title: Does Traversal Order Matter? A Systematic Study of Tree Traversal Methods in Transformer Grammars

author.name: Zongru Liu, Pengyu Ji, Pengcheng Wang, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: This work systematically studies tree traversal methods in Transformer Grammars, introducing Breadth-First Traversal and a hybrid Production-Rule Traversal that combines structural lookahead with early lexical generation, beyond the standard Depth-First Traversal. It evaluates these across language modeling, syntactic generalization, and summarization.

entry.title: Cloze: An Open Research Platform for Studying Human-AI Conversations in Mental Health Contexts

author.name: Matthew Flathers, Francesco Cipriani, John Torous

entry.summary: Cloze is an open-source platform for running controlled, monitored studies of human-AI conversation in mental health research, offering configurable models, prompts, scheduling, and unconditional safety constraints with full provenance logging. It addresses the lack of experimental control in consumer LLM products for researchers. Valuable infrastructure for responsible mental-health AI study.

entry.title: Focus When Necessary: Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Grounding for Training-Free Visual Grounding

author.name: Yifan Wang, Peiming Li, Shiyu Li, Zhiyuan Hu, Xiaochen Yang, Wenming Yang, Yang Tang, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: LazyMCoT is a training-free framework that adaptively allocates visual grounding effort based on sample difficulty using an uncertainty-based adaptive routing mechanism from first-token statistics, avoiding indiscriminate image scaling and cropping. It targets fine-grained perception in high-resolution images by MLLMs. A practical efficiency-accuracy improvement for visual grounding.

entry.title: LLM-Powered Virtual Population for Demand Simulation and Pricing

author.name: Chengpiao Huang, Kaizheng Wang

entry.summary: This work develops an LLM-powered virtual population model that simulates demand for pricing decisions by representing customers as a finite mixture of personas, eliciting persona-level purchase probabilities from rich product text and images, and aggregating through calibrated mixture weights to yield demand distributions with uncertainty. It supports counterfactual pricing. An interesting LLM-for-economics application.

entry.title: Selection Without Signal, Recovery Through Expression: A Measurement Study of Post-Hoc Falsification Operators for Frozen Small Code Models

author.name: Mehmet Iscan

entry.summary: This measurement study evaluates 26 semantic post-hoc operators (selection, verification, repair, elimination, portfolios, sound vetoes) against Best-of-N for frozen small code models under a leakage-free matched-compute protocol, finding that none improve held-out accuracy on the tested benchmarks. It provides a sobering negative result for post-hoc remedies. Useful methodological caution.

entry.title: FATE: Pillar Encoding and Frequency-Aware Training for Event-Based Object Detection

author.name: Md Tawheedul Islam Bhuian, Kyoung-Don Kang

entry.summary: FATE proposes a unified framework for event-based object detection built on a novel Pillar Encoding that preserves fine-grained temporal structure rather than discarding it through fixed temporal sub-binning, enabling frequency-aware training beyond the low temporal frequencies imposed by training supervision. It addresses the sparse, asynchronous nature of event streams. Relevant for event-camera perception.

entry.title: RAVA: Retrieval-Augmented Viewpoint Alignment for Subject-Driven Image Generation

author.name: Qiwei Yan, Zhiqiang Yuan, Chongyang Li, Jiapei Zhang, Ying Deng, Jinchao Zhang, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: RAVA addresses cross-subject viewpoint alignment in subject-driven image generation, where a model must infer one subject's implicit viewpoint and transfer it to another using only image-level evidence without camera poses or depth, using a retrieval-augmented approach to avoid spurious semantic correlations that cause viewpoint drift and structural mismatches. It targets reliable viewpoint control. Relevant for controllable generation.

entry.title: MaineCoon: Pursuing A Real-Time Audio-Visual Social World Model

author.name: Lichen Bai, Tianhao Zhang, Shitong Shao, Dingwei Tan, Qiyu Zhong, Zhengpeng Xie, Haopeng Li, Qinghao Huang, Dandan Shen, Tengjiao Ji, Wei Wang, Peicheng Wu, Yuxuan Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Welly Luo, Shurui Yang, Zeke Xie

entry.summary: MaineCoon presents a 22B-parameter real-time audio-visual autoregressive world model targeting human-centric social dynamics rather than physical or gaming worlds. It claims sub-second interaction latency as a prototype social world model.

entry.title: AnnotateAnything: Automatic Annotation of 3D Assets for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Haoran Lu, Mutian Shen, Shuyang Yu, Yu Xiao, Songling Liu, Jianshu Zhang, Shang Wu, Yue Chen, Guo Ye, Jiayi Wang, Zhaoran Wang, Han Liu

entry.summary: AnnotateAnything automatically converts passive 3D assets into manipulation-ready assets by inferring semantics, interaction constraints, and 3D-grounded cues via vision-language reasoning, plus a fully automatic annotation pipeline. It addresses the gap between raw geometry and actionable robot manipulation labels.

entry.title: Structured Adversarial Camouflage via Voronoi Diagrams

author.name: Jens Bayer, Stefan Becker, David M\"unch, Michael Arens, J\"urgen Beyerer

entry.summary: Proposes adversarial camouflage using Voronoi diagrams that optimizes only seed-point locations under fixed printable palettes, producing structured patterns that fool person detectors. The attack transfers across detector families and backgrounds in black-box settings.

entry.title: A Neuromorphic Trigger for Efficient Audio Event Detection

author.name: Benjamin Hatton, Oliver Rhodes, Luca Peres

entry.summary: Introduces a spiking neural network trigger that gates audio input, forwarding only salient segments to heavier downstream models for event detection. Achieves strong F1 scores while reducing computation for resource-constrained systems.

entry.title: Non-negative Elastic Net Decoding for Information Retrieval

author.name: Koki Okajima, Yasutoshi Ida, Tsukasa Yoshida, Yasuaki Nakamura

entry.summary: Reformulates dense retrieval as a joint decoding problem using non-negative elastic net optimization to select documents with awareness of the entire corpus, reducing redundancy. Aims to produce more diverse, less redundant retrieved sets than score-independent top-k.

entry.title: Expanding SPHERE-JEPA: A Family of Statistical Regularizers for the Hypersphere

author.name: L\'eo Nicollier (CB, ATT), Enric Meinhardt-Llopis (CB), Max Dunitz (ATT), Marc Pic (ATT), Pablo Mus\'e (CB, IFUMI), Gabriele Facciolo (CB)

entry.summary: This paper expands the SPHERE-JEPA family of self-supervised learning regularizers by analytically integrating out random projections to yield a deterministic Maximum Mean Discrepancy, avoiding the variance of sliced methods. It targets representation collapse prevention on the hypersphere.

entry.title: Where Should Action Generation Begin? A Learnable Source Prior for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Meipo Dai, Qiyuan Zhuang, He-Yang Xu, Ying-Jie Shuai, Yijun Wang, Qi Dou, Xiu-Shen Wei

entry.summary: LeaP replaces the standard Gaussian source distribution in generative robot policies with a proprioception-conditioned diagonal Gaussian over action chunks. This observation-informed yet stochastic initialization lets the generator focus on precise action refinement.

entry.title: GRACE-DS: a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science

author.name: Aleksandr Tsymbalov, Danis Zaripov, Artem Epifanov, Anastasya Palienko

entry.summary: GRACE-DS is a guarded reward-guided evaluation environment for LLM-powered AutoML agents on tabular ML tasks, with hidden validators measuring not only predictive performance but also leakage avoidance, reproducibility, protocol validity, and correction behavior. It supports pre-deployment evaluation across realistic data science workflow stages.

entry.title: XAI-Grounded Explanation Generation for Speech Deepfake Detection with Training-Free Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yupei Li, Qiyang Sun, Xiaoliang Wu, Chenxi Wang, Berrak Sisman, Bj\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free framework integrating XAI attribution evidence with multimodal LLMs to generate grounded natural-language explanations for speech deepfake detection. It bridges low-level attribution signals and human-understandable explanations without task-specific supervision.

entry.title: SkillWiki: A Living Knowledge Infrastructure for Agent Skills

author.name: Dingcheng Huang, Yuda Ding, Bingshuo Liu, Qingbin Liu, Xi Chen, Jiang Bian, Hongliang Sun, Zhiying Tu, Dianhui Chu, Xiaoyan Yu, Dianbo Sui

entry.summary: SkillWiki is a living knowledge infrastructure for agent skills supporting large-scale production, governance, and evolution by transforming heterogeneous knowledge into reusable skill assets linked to originating evidence. It presents a complete skill lifecycle from ingestion through provenance-aware exploration and execution-driven evolution.

entry.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation

author.name: Rutherford A. Patamia, Ming Liu, Wei Luo, Favour Ekong, Akan Cosgun

entry.summary: This work proposes an audio-only two-stage pipeline for multiparty turn-taking that separates when to trigger a turn boundary from whether the floor is actually transferring, with a fast trigger and lightweight verifier plus diffusion augmentation. It targets realistic multiparty audio with overlap and rapid speaker changes.

entry.title: Robust Dual-Signal Fusion: Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Gating with Compressed Chain-of-Thought Refinement for Irony Detection in Social Media Texts

author.name: Ankit Bhattacharjee, Krityapriya Bhaumik

entry.summary: The RDS Fusion framework is a hybrid neuro-symbolic architecture for zero-shot irony detection that compresses chain-of-thought reasoning without supervised fine-tuning, achieving 78.1% accuracy on TweetEval and filtering out-of-distribution hallucinations on iSarcasm. It matches fine-tuned BERTweet performance while remaining zero-shot.

entry.title: IMPACTeen: Intentions, Manipulation, Persuasion, Annotations, and Consequences in Teen Communication Dataset

author.name: Aleksander Szcz\k{e}sny, Wiktoria Mieleszczenko-Kowszewicz, Maciej Markiewicz, Beata Bajcar, Tomasz Adamczyk, Jolanta Babiak, Grzegorz Chodak, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko

entry.summary: IMPACTeen is a dataset of 1,021 social influence scenarios in adolescent contexts with 5,100 annotation records labeled from five perspectives (teens, parents, psychologists, communication experts, teachers). It supports research on social influence, manipulation, and persuasion detection in teen communication.

entry.title: Whose hotel does the AI recommend? An algorithm audit of reputation signals in LLM-assisted hotel selection

author.name: Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Asher Ali

entry.summary: This algorithm audit uses a pre-registered randomized conjoint design across personas, prompts, and twelve open and proprietary models to measure which reputation signals drive LLM hotel recommendations. It finds guest rating and price dominate, with a top rating raising selection by 31.6 percentage points. Relevant for understanding LLMs as commercial gatekeepers and bias.

entry.title: Reasoning Text-to-Video Retrieval for Operating Room Clips via Action-Driven Digital Twins

author.name: Yiqing Shen, Hao Ding, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: OR3 is a reasoning-capable text-to-video retrieval method for operating-room clips that converts clips into action-driven digital twins by grouping concurrent subject-action-object triplets under non-overlapping temporal intervals, enabling implicit queries requiring reasoning rather than relying on global embeddings. It supports OR safety event retrieval. A focused medical video retrieval contribution.

entry.title: EventDrive: Event Cameras for Vision-Language Driving Intelligence

author.name: Dongyue Lu, Rong Li, Ao Liang, Lingdong Kong, Wei Yin, Lai Xing Ng, Benoit R. Cottereau, Camille Simon Chane, Wei Tsang Ooi

entry.summary: EventDrive is a benchmark and model suite unifying event-camera streams, RGB frames, and language supervision for vision-language driving intelligence. It examines how high-dynamic-range, low-latency event sensing aids reasoning and decision-making across the driving loop.

entry.title: HumanoidArena: Benchmarking Egocentric Hierarchical Whole-body Learning

author.name: Taowen Wang, Zikang Xie, Bin Yang, Yunheng Wang, Zizhao Yuan, Yuetong Fang, Yixiao Feng, Yichi Wang, Xingyu Chen, Haodong Chen, Qiwei Wu, Weisheng Xu, Lihan Chen, Lusong Li, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: HumanoidArena is a simulation-first benchmark for egocentric hierarchical whole-body humanoid learning that specifically evaluates the high-level-policy-to-low-level-tracker interface for executability, robustness, and transferability. It addresses a gap where benchmarks rarely test the policy-tracker interface itself.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction Intervals with Tail-Specific Guarantees

author.name: Simone Cuonzo, Nina Deliu

entry.summary: This paper extends split conformal prediction to provide explicitly calibrated tail-specific coverage guarantees for upper and lower tails separately, then derives a two-sided interval by intersection with proven tail and global marginal coverage. It covers both exchangeable (finite-sample) and non-exchangeable (asymptotic) settings.

entry.title: Distributed General-Purpose Agent Networks: Architecture, Key Mechanisms, and Prototypes

author.name: Shengli Zhang, Deen Ma, Zibin Lin, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: Studies distributed peer-to-peer networks of heterogeneous LLM agents that discover one another, establish trust, and negotiate cooperation across devices and governance boundaries. Argues such networks need new mechanisms beyond combining existing P2P overlays with agents.

entry.title: SegTME-UNI2: A Foundation Model-Based Framework for Generalisable Multiclass Cell Segmentation and LLM-Driven Tumour Microenvironment Characterisation in Histopathology

author.name: Wan Siti Halimatul Munirah Wan Ahmad, Faris Syahmi Samidi, Mohammad Badal Ahmmed, Vimal Angela Thiviyanathan, Selvam James Thavaraj, Anwar P. P. Abdul Majeed

entry.summary: Presents a unified histopathology framework combining a pathology foundation model with dual UperNet decoders for multiclass cell segmentation and LLM-driven tumour microenvironment reporting. It addresses the lack of pixel-level annotations via progressive pseudo-labeling.

entry.title: Performance-Driven Environment Abstraction with Multi-Timescale Learning

author.name: Yue Guan, Dipankar Maity, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: This paper develops performance-driven environment abstraction for large MDPs, aggregating states to directly optimize decision quality rather than preserving structure. It pairs this with a multi-timescale RL framework with theoretical performance guarantees.

entry.title: Toward Controllable Catalyst Inverse Design via Large-Scale Autoregressive Pretraining

author.name: Dong Hyeon Mok, Jonggeol Na, Seoin Back

entry.summary: This work presents a GPT-based conditional generative model for inverse design of heterogeneous catalysts, using a numerical embedding layer to generate structures with target properties. It aims to overcome screening inefficiencies in catalyst discovery.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Neural Networks for Improved Short-Term Weather Forecasting: A Case Study over the South Pacific

author.name: Egor Bugaev, Fedor Buzaev, Dmitry Efremenko, Denis Derkach, Fedor Ratnikov

entry.summary: This study enhances physics-constrained neural networks for short-term weather forecasting over the South Pacific, building on WeatherGFT with an upgraded WENO-5 solver, a unified autoregressive hybrid block, and integration with foundation models. It achieves up to 26% MSE reduction.

entry.title: Monotonic Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: A Theoretical and Empirical Study of Monotonicity as an Inductive Bias

author.name: Mikhail Krasnov, Carolina Fortuna, Bla\v{z} Bertalani\v{c}

entry.summary: MKAN is a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network with hard monotonicity guaranteed for all parameter values via exponential reparameterization of B-spline coefficients. It enables standard unconstrained training while ensuring monotonicity, unlike prior projection-based methods.

entry.title: RadSEM: A Finding-by-Finding Metric for Clinical Consistency in Radiology Reports

author.name: Zhenhong Yang, Zhuoyun Liu, Jintao Fei, Wen Tang, Shichao Quan, Jun Zhao, Jun Xu

entry.summary: RadSEM is a finding-by-finding metric for evaluating radiology reports that distinguishes clinical compatibility from surface similarity, handling negation, laterality, and polarity. It performs contradiction-constrained matching of atomic finding sentences.

entry.title: Root-Selecting Fixed-Point Inversion for Rectified Flows via Trajectory Straightness

author.name: Semin Kim, Jihwan Yoon, Seunghoon Hong
