author.name: Yan Dai, Negin Golrezaei, Patrick Jaillet

entry.summary: This paper formalizes embedding model routing as an adversarial contextual linear bandit with low-rank experts, where queries are contexts, items are actions, and embedding models are experts. It identifies a log-quadratic policy class and analyzes policy regret under realistic bandit feedback conditions.

entry.title: Inference-time Policy Steering via Vision and Touch

author.name: Yilin Wu, Zilin Si, Zeynep Temel, Oliver Kroemer, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: ViTaL is a visuo-tactile inference-time steering framework for pre-trained robot policies, formulated as bi-level optimization combining visual mode selection with tactile-guided diffusion editing for contact-rich manipulation. It augments vision-only verification with contact-force information.

entry.title: LatentGym: A Testbed For Cross-Task Experiential Learning With Controllable Latent Structure

author.name: Daksh Mittal, Tommaso Castellani, Thomson Yen, Naimeng Ye, Fangyu Wu, Minghui Chen, Tiffany Cai, Emmanouil Koukoumidis, William Zeng, Hongseok Namkoong

entry.summary: LatentGym is a controllable testbed for cross-task experiential learning where each environment is organized around a ground-truth latent variable governing shared structure across tasks. It provides metrics that separate exploration from exploitation to measure whether and why agents improve over sequences of related tasks.

entry.title: CHILLGuard: Towards Fine-Grained Chinese LLM Safety Guardrail with Scalable Data Construction and Model-aware Preference Alignment

author.name: Wenbo Yu, Bohua Wang, Hao Fang, Kuofeng Gao, Jingru Zeng, Xiaochen Yang, Tianyi Zhang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Jiawei Kong, Hao Wu, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia, Min Zhang

entry.summary: CHILLGuard introduces a fine-grained Chinese LLM safety guardrail with a 5-macro/31-micro risk taxonomy, scalable data construction, and model-aware preference alignment. Addresses gaps in Chinese-specific regulatory and cultural safety coverage.

entry.title: Bayesian 3D Steerable CNNs: Enabling Equivariance and Uncertainty Quantification Simultaneously

author.name: Abhishek Keripale, Ponkrshnan Thiagarajan, Susanta Ghosh

entry.summary: Proposes Bayesian Steerable CNNs that place posterior distributions over basis coefficients to achieve SE(3)-equivariance and uncertainty quantification simultaneously, decomposing predictive uncertainty into epistemic and aleatoric components. Trained via variational inference.

entry.title: Wasserstein Convergence of ODE-Based Samplers in Decentralized Diffusion Model via Velocity Field Decomposition

author.name: Chencheng Tang, Xuanyu Xue, Fangyikang Wang, Chao Zhang, Hubery Yin

entry.summary: Establishes Wasserstein-2 convergence guarantees for ODE-based samplers in decentralized diffusion models that use multiple local velocity-field experts with stochastic routing, which falls outside standard diffusion convergence analyses. Provides theoretical rate via velocity field decomposition.

entry.title: EgoPhys: Learning Generalizable Physics Models of Deformable Objects from Egocentric Video

author.name: Hyunjin Kim, Ri-Zhao Qiu, Guangqi Jiang, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: Presents EgoPhys, which constructs deformable physical digital twins from egocentric RGB-only video by distilling per-object inverse-physics solutions into a compact codebook. Enables prediction of dense spring stiffness fields for unseen deformable objects without per-spring optimization.

entry.title: PACT: Privileged Trace Co-Training for Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Zhenbang Du, Jun Luo, Zhiwei Zheng, Xiangchi Yuan, Kejing Xia, Dachuan Shi, Qirui Jin, Qijia He, Shaofeng Zou, Yingbin Liang, Wenke Lee

entry.summary: Proposes PACT, a privileged trace co-training framework for multi-turn tool-use agents that uses expert traces only as training-time optimization signals while keeping rollout generation prompt-only. Aims to combine dense process supervision with avoiding over-constraining to fixed trajectories.

entry.title: SDS-LoRA: Overcoming Anisotropic Gradient Scaling in Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Junghun Oh, Sungyong Baik, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: Analyzes LoRA from a geometric perspective, showing that backpropagated full fine-tuning gradients undergo anisotropic scaling driven by singular values that distorts updates and reduces effective rank. Proposes SDS-LoRA to overcome this anisotropic gradient scaling.

entry.title: VeriGraph: Towards Verifiable Data-Analytic Agents

author.name: Jiajie Jin, Zhao Yang, Wenle Liao, Yuyang Hu, Guanting Dong, Xiaoxi Li, Yutao Zhu, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: VeriGraph is a neuro-symbolic framework that has data-analytic agents build explicit evidence DAGs during execution, separating deterministic computation from semantic deduction to make outputs auditable and reproducible. It targets verifiability of LLM analytical reasoning.

entry.title: Decision-Weighted Flow Matching for Contextual Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Jize Xie, Haomiao Wu, Qiang Chen, Xiu Su, Yi Chen

entry.summary: Decision-Weighted Flow Matching reweights the flow-matching velocity objective using decision-sensitive information so generated scenarios reduce downstream decision regret rather than just fitting the distribution. It aligns generative scenario modeling with contextual stochastic optimization.

entry.title: ATOM-Bench: A Real-World Benchmark for Atomic Skills and Compositional Generalization in Manipulation Policies

author.name: Zenan Wu, Bingqing Wei, Lu Liu, Zheqi He, Xi Wang, Jiakang Liu, Zehui Li, Guocai Yao, Jing-Shu Zheng, Xi Yang, Yongtao Wang

entry.summary: ATOM-Bench is a real-world manipulation benchmark factorizing tabletop tasks into motor and instruction atoms with 30 atomic and 24 held-out compositional tasks across single- and dual-arm robots. It diagnoses whether generalist policies can recombine learned skills in new structures.

entry.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents

author.name: Buqiang Xu, Zirui Xue, Dianmou Chen, Chenyang Fu, Chiyu Wu, Caiying Huang, Chen Jiang, Jizhan Fang, Xinle Deng, Yijun Chen, Yunzhi Yao, Xuehai Wang, Jin Shang, Gong Yu, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: TokenPilot is a dual-granularity context management framework for LLM agents that stabilizes prompt prefixes via ingestion-aware compaction and uses lifecycle-aware eviction to reduce tokens while preserving prompt-cache continuity. It resolves the trade-off between text sparsity and cache invalidation in long sessions.

entry.title: Repeated Bilateral Trade: The Quest for Fairness

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois Bachoc, Roberto Colomboni, Emilie Kaufmann

entry.summary: Studies repeated bilateral trade from a fairness angle, showing natural fairness desiderata yield a one-parameter Rawls-to-Nash family of fair-gain objectives via Holder means. Analyzes the new statistical/learning structure these objectives induce.

entry.title: Re-feeding Is Not Replaying: Measuring Replay Noise in Counterfactual Token-Credit Estimation

author.name: Nils Matteson

entry.summary: Measures the noise introduced by re-feeding transcript prefixes versus resuming from the verified decode-time KV state in per-token counterfactual credit estimation for LLM rollouts. Shows that at low-margin decision tokens, re-feeding meaningfully changes results, undermining a common assumption.

entry.title: How to Score Experts for One-Shot MoE Expert Pruning: A Unified Formulation and Selection Principle

author.name: Zongfang Liu, Jinghui Zhang, Zijian Ma, Guangyi Chen, Xin Yuan

entry.summary: Provides a unified formulation for one-shot MoE expert pruning organized around routing frequency, gate weighting, and activation strength, yielding a principled criteria-selection rule tied to deployment objectives. Addresses the heuristic, non-universal nature of existing pruning criteria.

entry.title: When Confidence Lacks Concepts: Interpretable OOD Detection via Representation Perturbations

author.name: Anju Chhetri, Pratik Shrestha, Ramesh Rana, Prashnna Gyawali, Binod Bhattarai

entry.summary: Proposes an interpretable OOD detection framework for medical imaging that probes prediction stability under class-conditioned semantic perturbations, using sparse autoencoders to learn class-specific concept vectors. Provides semantically meaningful OOD signals rather than opaque confidence scores.

entry.title: CacheMuon: Using Temporal Preconditioning To Approximate Polar Factor

author.name: Bishnu Dev (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE), Sushil Bohara (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE), Martin Tak\'a\v{c} (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE), Samuel Horv\'ath (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE)

entry.summary: CacheMuon exploits temporal correlation in the smoothly-changing momentum matrix of the Muon optimizer to reuse polar-factor information across steps, reducing the cost of per-step Newton-Schulz iterations. This temporal preconditioning approximates the polar factor more cheaply.

entry.title: PhysGuard: Fisher-Guided Gradient Projection for Sim-to-Real Neural PDE Surrogates

author.name: Changjian Zhou, Junfeng Fang, Negin Yousefpour, Peng Wu, Bin Yan, Guillermo A Narsilio

entry.summary: PhysGuard uses Fisher-guided gradient projection to adapt neural PDE surrogates from simulation to real measurements while preserving core physics representations learned during pretraining. It addresses the sim-to-real gap for neural operators.

entry.title: Distribution Alignment for One-Shot Federated Learning via Optimal Transport

author.name: Daniele Berardini (AI for Good), Vito Paolo Pastore (AI for Good, MaLGa-DIBRIS, University of Genoa, Genoa, Italy), Vittorio Murino (AI for Good, Department of Computer Science, University of Verona, Verona, Italy)

entry.summary: SLOT-Align is a learning-free optimal transport framework for one-shot federated learning that harmonizes feature representations across clients with both domain and label shift. It uses a shared frozen encoder and single-round alignment.

entry.title: Polynomial-Time Mistake-Bounded Language Generation

author.name: H\'ector Jimenez, Alexander Kozachinskiy, Vicente Opazo

entry.summary: Introduces a polynomial-time version of the mistake-bounded language generation framework, proving that monotone Boolean functions with polynomially-many maxterms are polynomial-time MBLG. Presents the technique as a combinatorial game about writing numbers on a board.

entry.title: Graphical conditional generative modeling for digital twin modeling

author.name: Zongren Zou, Th\'eo Bourdais, Ricardo Baptista, Houman Owhadi

entry.summary: Introduces a graphical conditional generative modeling framework for digital twins that discovers parsimonious surrogate variables by identifying which inputs influence the full conditional law (not just the mean) of target quantities. Aims to build interpretable, maintainable stochastic surrogates.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Personalization via Semantic Constraint Verification

author.name: Xuran Li, Guanqin Zhang, Imran Razzak, Hakim Hacid, Eleanna Kafeza, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: Introduces NLICV, a natural language inference based framework for evaluating LLM personalization by mapping sentence meanings to truth-condition sets and categorizing behaviors into personalization, generalization, sycophancy, and failure. Offers a scalable, interpretable alternative to surface-matching and LLM-as-judge metrics.

entry.title: Elastic ODYN: Differentiable Optimization for Infeasible Control and Learning in Robotics

author.name: Aristotelis Papatheodorou, Jose Rojas, Ioannis Havoutis, Carlos Mastalli

entry.summary: Presents Elastic ODYN, a primal-dual non-interior-point QP solver that handles infeasible quadratic programs in robotics via smooth squared-L2 elastic relaxations, remaining well-posed under ill-conditioning and converging to closest-to-feasible solutions. Supports warm-starting and differentiable use in control and learning.

entry.title: Sobolev Approximation by Fixed-Size Neural Networks with Arbitrary Accuracy

author.name: Baicheng Li, Haizhao Yang, Shijun Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates new activation functions enabling fixed-size neural networks to achieve arbitrary-accuracy Sobolev-norm approximation, introducing a smooth Differentiable Universal Activation Function. Proves any function in a given Sobolev space can be approximated to arbitrary accuracy in a corresponding lower-order norm by a fixed-size network.

entry.title: Encode Errors: Representational Retrieval of In-Context Demonstrations for Multilingual Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Guangyue Peng, Wei Li, Wen Luo, Houfeng Wang

entry.summary: Extracts a Grammatical Error Representation from LLM internal states to retrieve in-context demonstrations capturing error patterns rather than semantic similarity for multilingual GEC. It improves few-shot GEC by better demonstration selection.

entry.title: AthDGC: An Open Diachronic Greek Treebank with Indo-European Parallels

author.name: Nikolaos Lavidas, Kiki Nikiforidou, Dag Haug, Leonid Kulikov, Vassiliki Geka, Vassileios Symeonidis, Theodoros Michalareas, Sofia Chionidi, Anastasia Tsiropina, Eleni Plakoutsi, Evangelos Argyropoulos

entry.summary: AthDGC is the first openly licensed dependency-parsed Greek treebank spanning eight diachronic periods under a single schema, with verse-level New Testament alignment to Latin, Gothic, Old Church Slavonic, and Armenian. It provides an end-to-end annotation workflow.

entry.title: Beyond NL2Code: A Structured Survey of Multimodal Code Intelligence

author.name: Xuanle Zhao, Qiushi Sun, Jingyu Xiao, Xuexin Liu, Haoyue Yang, Qiaosheng Chen, Xianzhen Luo, Jing Huang, Yufeng Zhong, Lei Chen, Shuai Fu, Zhenlin Wei, Jinhe Bi, Lei Jiang, Haibo Qiu, Siqi Yang, Peng Shi, Jian Hu, Zhixiong Zeng

entry.summary: A structured survey of multimodal code intelligence covering systems that generate, edit, refine, execute, or reason with code from visual artifacts like screenshots, charts, and videos. It organizes the field by the role code plays in each task.

entry.title: Can LLM Coding Agents Reason About Time Series?

author.name: Filip Rechtor\'ik, Ond\v{r}ej Du\v{s}ek, Zden\v{e}k Kasner

entry.summary: Examines whether LLM coding agents can reason about time series by comparing raw-data input, code-agent querying, and combined approaches on two benchmarks. It finds code-access agents outperform raw-data processing by up to 10% but still err on 22-34% of questions.

entry.title: Contrastive-Difference CKA Reveals Concept-Specific Structural Alignment Across Language Model Architectures

author.name: Xueping Gao

entry.summary: This work introduces contrastive-difference CKA, a training-free diagnostic showing that different LLM architectures encode high-level concepts with moderate geometric convergence but near-perfect functional transferability. It documents a geometric-functional universality dissociation across concept domains.

entry.title: Cloze: An Open Research Platform for Studying Human-AI Conversations in Mental Health Contexts

author.name: Matthew Flathers, Francesco Cipriani, John Torous

entry.summary: Cloze is an open-source web platform for conducting controlled, monitored studies of human-AI conversation in mental health research, giving researchers experimental control over models, prompts, scheduling, and safety constraints. Every message is captured with full provenance.

entry.title: Focus When Necessary: Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Grounding for Training-Free Visual Grounding

author.name: Yifan Wang, Peiming Li, Shiyu Li, Zhiyuan Hu, Xiaochen Yang, Wenming Yang, Yang Tang, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: LazyMCoT is a training-free framework that adaptively allocates visual grounding effort based on sample difficulty, using an adaptive routing mechanism with first-token uncertainty statistics. It avoids computational redundancy on simple queries while preserving accuracy on complex high-resolution images.

entry.title: GridVQA-X: A Framework for Evaluating Multimodal Explainability Methods

author.name: Sujay Belsare, Sudarshan Nikhil, Sushant Kumar, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: GridVQA-X is a framework for evaluating multimodal explainability methods, providing ground truth to distinguish true cross-modal reasoning from shallow shortcuts like bag-of-words matching. It addresses the lack of evaluation protocols for whether explanations capture synergistic cross-modal interactions.

entry.title: Physics-Driven Zero-Shot MRI Reconstruction with Non-local Image Priors

author.name: Lingtong Zhang, Wenlei Li, Mu He, Li Xiao, Yang Ji

entry.summary: This paper proposes a physics-driven zero-shot self-supervised MRI reconstruction framework that combines physical consistency with image-domain nonlocal priors. It introduces a coil-sensitivity-guided dynamic repository to stabilize training from a single undersampled scan.

entry.title: Focus, Align, and Sustain: Counteracting Gradient Dilution in Incremental Object Detection

author.name: Aoting Zhang, Dongbao Yang, Chang Liu, Xiaopeng Hong, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: This work identifies Gradient Dilution as the root cause of performance degradation when adapting Detection Transformers to incremental object detection, decomposing it into signal dispersion, assignment drift, and support attrition. It proposes mechanisms to focus, align, and sustain preservation gradients.

entry.title: G2IA: Geometry-Guided Instance-Aware Retrieval and Refinement for Cross-Modal Place Recognition

author.name: Xianyun Jiao, Jingyi Xu, Zhongmiao Yan, Xieyuanli Chen, Lin Pei

entry.summary: G2IA is a geometry-guided instance-aware framework for cross-modal place recognition that localizes camera-only robots against pre-built LiDAR maps. It combines geometry-aware representation alignment with fine-grained instance-level candidate verification to address the modality gap and perceptual aliasing.

entry.title: Task-Instructed Causal Routing of Vision Foundation Models for Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Donghyun Han, Yuseok Bae, Jung Uk Kim, Hyung-Il Kim

entry.summary: TIGER coordinates multiple heterogeneous vision foundation models for multi-task dense prediction via task-instruction-guided causal expert routing, rather than naively aggregating expert features. Leverages natural-language task instructions to route to complementary experts.

entry.title: OmniOPSD: Rationale-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Affective Computing

author.name: Zebang Cheng, Shuimu Chen, Boxue Yang, Yuanshen Guan, Jingyi Chen, Zheng Lian, Xiaojiang Peng, Fei Ma, LaiZhong Cui, Qi Tian

entry.summary: OmniOPSD uses rationale-privileged on-policy self-distillation to address reward sparsity in RL for multimodal LLMs on human-centered affective reasoning, improving transparency over direct label-based fine-tuning. Targets emotions, intentions, and behaviors with safety considerations.

entry.title: Stepwise Token Selection for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Landi He, Shawn Young, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: Reformulates visual token pruning in multimodal LLMs as a sequential decision process with a pointer-style selection mechanism that conditions each choice on previous ones and learns when to stop, replacing fixed top-k independent scoring. Improves efficiency where visual prefix dominates inference cost.

entry.title: Learned JPEG Compression for DNN Vision

author.name: Kaixiang Zheng, Ahmed H. Salamah, Siyu Chen, En-Hui Yang

entry.summary: J4D is a training framework that learns JPEG encoding parameters to minimize compression rate while maximizing downstream DNN inference performance, using a differentiable representation of the JPEG codec and rate. Optimizes a decades-old human-oriented codec for machine consumption.

entry.title: teasr: training-efficient any-step diffusion transformer for real-world image super-resolution

author.name: Xiang Gao, Chenxin Zhu, Yushun Fang, Qiang Hu, Xiaoyun Zhang

entry.summary: TEASR is a training-efficient any-step diffusion framework for real-world image super-resolution that supports one-step and multi-step restoration in a unified model via self-adversarial distillation, eliminating auxiliary teacher models. Enables flexible speed-quality tradeoffs.

entry.title: Output-Level Regularization Eliminates the Seed Lottery in Single-GPU VLA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jeffrin Sam, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: This work identifies a seed lottery in single-GPU VLA fine-tuning where identical code with different random seeds silently produces a 29 percentage-point success gap due to output collapse, where the action predictor learns near-identical outputs regardless of observation. It shows weight-level methods like L2 and EWC are structurally blind to this collapse and proposes output-level regularization to eliminate it.

entry.title: Self-Improving VLA Policies: Selected Diffusion Noise for Spurious-Robust Action Smoothing

author.name: Duc Minh Nguyen, Bao-Ngoc Dao, Tung M. Luu, Binh Gia Nguyen, Vinh Tong, Anji Liu, Vu N. Duong, Dung D. Le, Daniel Sonntag, Trung Le, Ngan Le, Jan Peter, An Thai Le, Minh Nhat Vu, Mathias Niepert, Khoa D. Doan, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien Anh Ngo

entry.summary: Introduces Selected Diffusion Noise (SDN), a training-free test-time method that improves robustness of diffusion-based VLA manipulation policies by sampling diverse noise vectors to reduce reliance on spurious visual cues. It improves both robustness and success rate under perturbations.

entry.title: When and How Severely: Scenario-Specific Safety Envelopes for Driving VLAs

author.name: Abhinaw Priyadershi, Jelena Frtunikj

entry.summary: Evaluates safety envelopes for the 10B-parameter open-weight Alpamayo R1 driving VLA across nearly 16,000 clip-attack pairs, revealing a conservative-aggregate gap where aggregate thresholds mask scenario-specific tolerances. It builds scenario-specific severity bands under SOTIF/ISO 21448 framing.

entry.title: CADET: Physics-Grounded Causal Auditing and Training-Free Deconfounding of End-to-End Driving Planners

author.name: Zikun Guo

entry.summary: CADET is a training-free framework for physics-grounded causal auditing and deconfounding of already-deployed end-to-end driving planners, detecting reliance on spurious cues that standard open-loop metrics miss. It enables auditing without retraining large models.

entry.title: Optimal Multiscale Learning of Linear Operators

author.name: Jiaheng Chen, Daniel Sanz-Alonso

entry.summary: Establishes statistical and computational limits for learning bounded linear operators between Sobolev spaces from noisy data, recasting the problem in wavelet coordinates as multiscale matrix regression and constructing a minimax-optimal blockwise least-squares estimator. It exploits nonuniform per-scale difficulty for scale-adaptive sample allocation.

entry.title: Dr-DCI: Scaling Direct Corpus Interaction via Dynamic Workspace Expansion

author.name: Yi Lu, Zhuofeng Li, Ping Nie, Haoxiang Zhang, Yuyu Zhang, Kai Zou, Wenhu Chen, Jimmy Lin, Dongfu Jiang, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: DR-DCI extends Direct Corpus Interaction by treating retrieval as an agent-callable action to scale shell-executable corpus operations without the slowness of full-corpus terminal commands. It addresses efficiency limits in agentic search over large corpora.

entry.title: Feature Attribution in Directed Acyclic Graphs Using Edge Intervention

author.name: Qiheng Sun, Junxu Liu, Xiaokai Mao, Haocheng Xia, Jinfei Liu, Kui Ren, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: Mask-Proof is an LLM-based pipeline that converts real mathematical proofs into automatically checkable masked-step tasks, evaluating step-level reasoning across diverse sources. Aims to scalably measure proof reasoning beyond final answers.

entry.title: APEX: Adaptive Principle EXtraction A Three-Layer Self-Evolution Framework for Production AI Agents

author.name: Ya-Chuan Chen, Tien-Jen Lai, Hsiang-Wei Hu

entry.summary: APEX is a three-layer co-evolution framework for self-improving production AI agents that simultaneously evolves the prompt harness, behavioral principles, and workflow topology, extending prior single-dimension self-improvement methods. Reports gains on Terminal-Bench-style tasks.

entry.title: ToolMenuBench: Benchmarking Tool-Menu Filtering Strategies for Reliable and Efficient LLM Agents

author.name: Rahul Suresh Babu, Laxmipriya Ganesh Iyer

entry.summary: ToolMenuBench benchmarks how the visible tool menu (size, distractors, risk exposure) shapes reliability, efficiency, and safety in multi-step LLM agents, beyond just whether tools are called correctly. Reports filter-level and downstream metrics across seven backends.

entry.title: Multi-agent Framework for Time-Sensitive Complementary Collaboration in Minecraft

author.name: Juheon Yi, Jinglu Wang, Xiaoyi Zhang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: TickingCollabBench is a Minecraft-based multi-agent benchmark for time-sensitive complementary collaboration tasks featuring agent heterogeneity, mandatory collaboration, dynamic environments, and real-time constraints. Includes a framework for automated benchmark generation.

entry.title: Rethinking Scaffolding in LLM Tutors: The Interactional Mismatch Between Benchmarks and Real-World Deployments

author.name: Alexandra Neagu, Jeffrey T. H. Wong, Marcus Messer, Rhodri Nelson, Peter B. Johnson

entry.summary: Critiques the mismatch between AI tutor benchmarks that assume high student uptake of scaffolding and real-world deployments where students engage differently, analyzing nearly 9,500 chats with Chatbot Scaffolding and Student Uptake metrics. Questions a core assumption in educational AI evaluation.

entry.title: Rhythm of the Deep: A Computational-Linguistic Test of Duality of Patterning in Sperm Whale Codas

author.name: Mudit Sinha, Sanika Chavan

entry.summary: Tests whether sperm whale codas exhibit duality of patterning (the two-level combinatorial structure of human language) using 1,483 codas and a consensus of frozen audio encoders with held-out structural tests. Finds support for a narrow two-tier architecture while controlling for acoustic imitation.

entry.title: TimeVista: Exploring and Exploiting Vision-Language Models as Judges for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Zhi Chen, Yuxuan Wang, Jialong Wu, Yong Liu, Haoran Zhang, Xingjian Su, Jianmin Wang, Mingsheng Long

entry.summary: Proposes using Vision-Language Models as judges to evaluate time series forecasting, combining micro and macro-level judgments grounded in textual context. Extends the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm to a domain where traditional point-wise metrics align poorly with human intuition.

entry.title: AdaSTORM: Scaling LLM Reasoning on Dynamic Graphs via Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Bing Hao, Ruijie Wang, Haodong Qian, Yunlong Chu, Yuhang Liu, Yumeng Lin, Minglai Shao, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: AdaSTORM scales LLM reasoning on large dynamic graphs by adaptive partitioning into subgraphs and spatio-temporal multi-agent collaboration, overcoming the tens-of-nodes ceiling of current models. Reformulates large-scale dynamic graph reasoning into partition-and-coordinate stages.

entry.title: ARB4WM: An Adversarial Robustness Benchmark for World Models in Continuous Control

author.name: Junjian Zhang, Hao Tan, Ruonan Li, Dong Zhu, Aiping Li, Zhaoquan Gu

entry.summary: ARB4WM is a unified adversarial robustness benchmark for world-model agents in continuous control, defining five white-box loss objectives across policy, value, and latent-dynamics levels under visual perturbations. Provides pre-deployment robustness and risk assessment for safety-critical world-model systems.

entry.title: OpenClaw-Skill: Collective Skill Tree Search for Agentic Large Language Models

author.name: Tianyi Lin, Chuanyu Sun, Jingyi Zhang, Changxu Wei, Huanjin Yao, Shunyu Liu, Xikun Zhang, Liu Liu, Jiaxing Huang

entry.summary: OpenClaw-Skill introduces Collective Skill Tree Search, a tree-search framework that jointly generates and assesses reusable skills via collective intelligence to enhance agentic LLMs in tool use and multi-step reasoning. Builds structured, diverse, generalizable skill trees automatically.

entry.title: When in Doubt, Plan It Out: Committed Small Language Model Deliberation for Reactive Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nathan Gavenski, Juarez Monteiro, Francisco Galuppo, Adriano Veloso, Odinaldo Rodrigues

entry.summary: PACT combines a fast reactive RL policy with a slow deliberative small language model planner that asynchronously generates and validates action plans, executing verified plans directly to bypass the RL policy in unfamiliar situations. Outperforms baselines on FrozenLake using only a 2B-parameter SLM.

entry.title: Is My Vision-Language Data in Your AI? Membership Inference Test (MINT) Demo 2

author.name: Daniel DeAlcala, Gonzalo Mancera, Julian Fierrez, Aythami Morales, Ruben Tolosana, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez

entry.summary: MINT Demo 2 presents a Membership Inference Test framework with multiple architectures to experimentally determine whether specific vision-language data were used in model training, achieving up to 90% detection accuracy across a face recognition model, four LLMs, and large image/text databases. Offers a web platform for training-data transparency auditing.

entry.title: Temporally Consistent and Controllable Video Generation of 2D Cine CMR via Latent Space Motion Modeling

author.name: Yiheng Cao (SyCoIA - IMT Mines Al\`es), Gustavo Andrade-Miranda (SyCoIA - IMT Mines Al\`es), Jiatian Zhang, Guillaume Sall\'e, Xin Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a text-to-video framework for synthesizing temporally coherent and anatomically consistent cine cardiac MRI by decoupling spatial structure from temporal motion, using a diffusion model for the initial frame and a latent flow model conditioned on cardiac phase for motion. Addresses public dataset scarcity for cardiac function assessment.

entry.title: JoyAI-VL-Interaction: Real-Time Vision-Language Interaction Intelligence

author.name: Dingyu Yao, Junhao Zhou, Chenxu Yang, Chuanyu Qin, Haowen Hou, Zheming Liang, Congcong Wang, Yuhang Cao, Shenglong Ye, Shuai Xie, Shuhuan Gu, Haoyang Huang, Qingyi Si, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: JoyAI-VL-Interaction argues for a proactive vision-language interaction paradigm where a model continuously watches a scene and autonomously decides when to speak or stay silent, rather than operating turn-by-turn. It targets real-time scenarios like security monitoring and livestreams with delegation to a background model for hard cases.

entry.title: Harnessing cortical geometry, wiring, and function as inductive biases for recurrent neural networks

author.name: Mo Shakiba, Rana Rokni, Mohammad Mohammadi, Nima Dehghani

entry.summary: This work uses the MICrONS functional connectomics dataset to build biologically grounded recurrent neural networks, initializing weights from real cortical connectivity, spatial coordinates, and function-derived relationships across ~12,000 neurons. It imposes communication-aware spatial constraints as inductive biases.

entry.title: AI Contagion in Social Networks

author.name: Olivier Bos, Stefano Bosi

entry.summary: This paper models how AI-generated content interacts with social communication networks, identifying an AI contagion channel and a social distortion multiplier through which retraining amplifies past errors. It reduces the high-dimensional system to a two-dimensional representation whose spectral radius determines stability of collective knowledge.

entry.title: HoloRec: Holistic Encoding and Interleaved Reasoning for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Shuqi Zhao, Jingsong Su, Xiang Liu, Xingzhi Yao, Yiming Qiu, Huimu Wang, Liang Lin, Pengbo Mo, Mingming Li, Jiao Dai, Jizhong Han, Songlin Hu

entry.summary: Introduces HoloRec, a generative recommendation method that unifies representation, reasoning, and generation via hierarchical nested residual quantization and an endogenous chain-of-thought, avoiding expensive external CoT annotations. Targets multi-step reasoning in recommender systems.

entry.title: Surprise-Guided MergeSort: Budget-Efficient Human-in-the-Loop Ranking via Adaptive Comparison Scheduling

author.name: Yujin Park, Haejun Chung, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: Surprise-Guided MergeSort uses a vision-language model as a question prioritizer (not annotator replacement) to identify which pairwise comparisons genuinely need human judgment, combining a MergeSort scheduler exploiting transitivity with surprise-based scheduling. Reduces human annotation cost for subjective ranking.

entry.title: Visualizing Uncertainty: Spatial Maps of Missing and Conflicting Evidence in Deep Learning

author.name: Dong Hyun Jeong, Feng Chen, Jin-Hee Cho, Lance M. Kaplan, Audun J{\o}sang, Soo-Yeon Ji

entry.summary: Proposes the Uncertainty Activation Map combining Evidential Deep Learning with Full-Gradient Class Activation Mapping to produce spatial maps distinguishing vacuity (lack of evidence) from dissonance (conflicting evidence). Provides interpretable spatial uncertainty for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Topological Flow Matching

author.name: Kacper Wyrwal, \.Ismail \.Ilkan Ceylan, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: Proposes topological flow matching, a generalization of flow matching that injects topological structure via a Laplacian-derived drift, framed as solving a degenerate Schrodinger bridge problem. Targets structured-domain signals such as fMRI on brain graphs.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation with Curriculum Turn-level Guidance for Multi-turn Agents

author.name: Gengsheng Li, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Ruiqi Liu, Tianyu Yang, Jie Sun, Qiyong Zhong, Haiyun Guo, Junfeng Fang, Dan Zhang, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a compounding-error failure mode in on-policy distillation for multi-turn agents and proposes Guided-OPD, which mixes teacher and student generations to keep trajectories within the teacher's reliable distribution. Aims to transfer large-model agentic capabilities to smaller students.

entry.title: AuAu: A Benchmark for Auditing Authoritarian Alignment in Large Language Models

author.name: Andreas Einwiller, Max Klabunde, Florian Lemmerich

entry.summary: Introduces AuAu, a benchmark auditing whether LLMs exhibit or promote authoritarian attitudes, combining validated psychometric instruments, behavioral vignettes, and realistic user prompts. Evaluates both general authoritarian closeness and established subconstructs.

entry.title: Calibrated Sampling-Free Uncertainty Estimation in Bayesian Deep Learning

author.name: Tobias Jan Wieczorek, Leon de Andrade, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Develops calibrated sampling-free uncertainty estimation for Bayesian deep learning via variance propagation in a single forward pass, extending the technique from MLPs to modern architectures. Avoids the prohibitive cost of averaging across many posterior-sampled forward passes.

entry.title: SPARK: Security Knowledge Priming and Representation-Guided Knowledge Activation for LLM-based Secure Code Generation

author.name: Xiaoyun Xu, Lichao Wu, Jona te Lintelo, Siyu Zhang, Stjepan Picek

entry.summary: Presents SPARK, an inference-time security harness that activates latent security knowledge already present in pretrained LLMs via brief representation-guided cues, without retraining or retrieval. Argues the bottleneck in secure code generation is activation rather than missing expertise.

entry.title: RL-Index: Reinforcement Learning for Retrieval Index Reasoning

author.name: Yongjia Lei, Nedim Lipka, Zhisheng Qi, Utkarsh Sahu, Koustava Goswami, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes RL-Index, an agentic indexing framework formulating retrieval index reasoning as a reinforcement learning problem, shifting reasoning to the knowledge corpus (index side) rather than the query side. Reduces online latency while handling implicit, complex query-knowledge relationships.

entry.title: Sycophancy as Material Failure under Pushback Loading: A Multi-Axis Characterization Across Three Loading Cases and up to Seventeen Material Charges

author.name: Ferdinand M. Schessl

entry.summary: This paper reframes LLM sycophancy as a materials-science failure under progressive pushback loading, characterizing stance-flips across thousands of conversation specimens with multi-axis turn-level measurements. It aims to resolve the low construct agreement plaguing sycophancy research.

entry.title: Follow the Latent Roadmap: Navigating Revocable Decoding for Diffusion LLMs with Anchor Tokens

author.name: Yizhen Yao, Qinglin Zhu, Runcong Zhao, Xiangxiang Dai, Yanzheng Xiang, Yulan He, Lin Gui

entry.summary: ASRD is a training-free framework for diffusion LLMs that decouples decoding context into trusted anchor tokens to prevent error propagation and local error reinforcement during revocable decoding. It improves the speed-quality trade-off of parallel generation.

entry.title: TuneJury: An Open Metric for Improving Music Generation Preference Alignment

author.name: Yonghyun Kim, Junwon Lee, Haiwen Xia, Yinghao Ma, Junghyun Koo, Koichi Saito, Yuki Mitsufuji, Chris Donahue

entry.summary: TuneJury is an open instance-level pairwise reward model for text-to-music that predicts preference scores from prompt and audio, trained on public human-preference labels and supporting data filtering and anchor calibration for new generators. It enables preference alignment in music generation.

entry.title: Size Doesn't Matter: Cosine-Scored Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Silen Naihin, Lev Stambler

entry.summary: This paper shows that BatchTopK sparse autoencoders let high-norm tokens inflate pre-activations and claim dictionary slots regardless of content alignment, and proposes replacing the inner-product score with a learned blend of cosine similarity and magnitude. The optimizer never recovers pure inner product, indicating norm is uninformative for feature detection.

entry.title: False Sense of Safety in Selective Signal Classification: Auditing Bound Tightness and Exchangeability for Risk Control

author.name: Jingwen Zhou, Mingzhe Wang

entry.summary: Audits distribution-free risk control for selective prediction in signal-domain detectors like anomalous-sound detection and AI-image forensics. Shows that common naive thresholding frequently violates declared error budgets, while certified bounds offer reliable but more conservative guarantees.

entry.title: Model Stealing Through the Lens of Model Multiplicity

author.name: Eliott Baltz, Satoshi Hara, Ulrich A\"ivodji

entry.summary: Examines model stealing through the lens of model multiplicity, arguing that query-based extraction yields many near-optimal surrogates differing in deployment-relevant properties beyond fidelity. Challenges the assumption that stolen surrogates grant economic leverage equal to the original service.

entry.title: Scalar-Stepsize Nonuniform Monte Carlo Optimistic Policy Iteration: A Certified Counterexample

author.name: Yuanlong Chen

entry.summary: Provides a certified negative answer to whether Monte Carlo optimistic policy iteration converges under nonuniform update frequencies with scalar stepsizes, constructing a three-state MDP counterexample with an attracting periodic orbit. Shows the recursion stays trapped near the cycle and fails to converge.

entry.title: Not all Jensen-Shannon Divergence Estimators are Equal

author.name: Alba Garrido, Alejandro Almod\'ovar, Mar Elizo, Patricia A. Apell\'aniz, Santiago Zazo, Juan Parras

entry.summary: Shows that Jensen-Shannon divergence estimates for synthetic tabular data fidelity are non-comparable across protocols: marginal-based estimators ignore joint dependencies and underestimate divergence, while classifier-based estimators capture structure but exhibit strong estimator dependence. Systematically studies this measurement problem across controlled settings.

entry.title: BRICKS-WM: Building Reusability via Interface Composition Kinetics for Structured World Models

author.name: Shaowei Zhang, Jiahan Cao, Xunlan Zhou, Shenghua Wan, De-Chuan Zhan

entry.summary: BRICKS-WM proposes a modular framework for building world models in model-based RL by composing independent entity dynamics, so that changing the agent does not require retraining the entire environment model. This addresses reusability limitations in monolithic latent dynamics for continuous control.

entry.title: We Need Explanation Cards to Connect Explanation Algorithms to the Real World

author.name: Eric G\"unther, Bal\'azs Szabados, Kristof Meding, Gunnar K\"onig, Sebastian Bordt, Ulrike von Luxburg

entry.summary: This position paper proposes Explanation Cards that augment standard algorithmic explanations with information about robustness, validity, and interpretation instructions. It aims to bridge the gap between what explanations appear to convey and what they actually provide.

entry.title: Filtered Conformal Ellipsoids for Graph-Native Time Series

author.name: Yannick Limmer

entry.summary: This paper proposes filtered conformal ellipsoids for multivariate time series, using a frozen state-space filter to shape the prediction region and split-conformal calibration for the radius. It analyzes coverage despite dependent filtered scores via contraction in an observable predictive-law quantity.

entry.title: Bridging data-driven priors via the score function for posterior sampling -- Comparative review and experimental study

author.name: Elhadji Cisse Faye, Mame Diarra Fall, Sylvain Delchini, Nicolas Dobigeon

entry.summary: This review unifies diverse data-driven priors used in Bayesian inverse problems (RED, normalizing flows, score-based models, convex-ridge regularizers) through their score functions. It demonstrates their integration into a common sampling algorithm on inpainting and super-resolution.

entry.title: VANDERER: Map-Free Exploration using Future-Aware and Visual-Curiosity-Guided Diffusion Policy

author.name: Venkata Naren Devarakonda, Raktim Gautam Goswami, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: VANDERER is a map-free exploration framework using a Visual Curiosity Module to guide pre-trained diffusion policies with only monocular images, avoiding occupancy-map generation. A navigation world model predicts action outcomes and a curiosity cost steers exploration.

entry.title: CREST: Deployment-Realistic Hardware-in-the-Loop NAS for Embedded Sensing Systems

author.name: Joseph Q. Zales, Pragya Sharma, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: CREST is a deployment-realistic hardware-in-the-loop neural architecture search framework for microcontroller sensing systems that uses real measured costs rather than FLOP proxies and deployed sensing schedules. It corrects mis-ranking of Pareto-front candidates from simplified assumptions.

entry.title: The Reverse Telescoping Coordinate System for Positive Definite Matrices: Geometry, Computation, and Generative Modeling

author.name: Anindya Bhadra

entry.summary: Proposes a new unconstrained coordinate system (reverse telescoping map) for representing symmetric positive definite matrices, decomposing them into log-determinant, shape, and partial covariance components. The construction yields a lossless symbolic representation of both a matrix and its inverse with favorable Jacobian properties for generative modeling.

entry.title: KeepLoRA++: Continual Learning with Layer-Scaled Residual Gradient Adaptation

author.name: Mao-Lin Luo, Yi-Lin Zhang, Zi-Hao Zhou, Yankun Hong, Xialiang Tong, Mingxuan Yuan, Tong Wei, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: Presents KeepLoRA++, a continual learning method for pretrained vision-language models that balances knowledge retention and plasticity via a dual-dimensional (inter-layer and intra-layer) retention mechanism with layer-scaled residual gradient adaptation. Analyzes how transferable knowledge is distributed across the Transformer.

entry.title: FEnc$^2$: Unifying Data Packing for Efficient Private Inference via Convolution and Architecture-Aware Fragment Encoding

author.name: Ran Ran, Zhaoting Gong, Nuo Xu, Yuanchao Xu, Fan Yao, Wujie Wen

entry.summary: Proposes FEnc2, a unified fragment-based ciphertext encoding framework for CKKS-based private CNN inference under fully homomorphic encryption, optimizing slot utilization, rotation complexity, and ciphertext counts simultaneously. Addresses inefficiencies in existing packing strategies that preserve only neighboring data or feature grouping.

entry.title: Beyond Artifacts: Towards Generalizable Synthetic Song Detection via Music-Intrinsic Features

author.name: Yan Han, Zhibin Wen, Yuan Wang, Shuangrun Shao, Xiaobing Li, Yang Xu, Wei Li

entry.summary: Proposes Sofia, a synthetic song detection framework that models music-intrinsic attributes (vocal, audio-effect, global structure) via feature-specific experts and an adaptive Mixture-of-Experts module, moving beyond low-level artifact detection. Constructs MUSIC8K, a challenging benchmark for generator-agnostic detection.

entry.title: Latent space mapping of interpretable structural coordinates from stochastic single-molecule signals

author.name: Matteo Cartiglia, Sandro Kuppel, Wouter Botermans Wannes Peeters, Natan Biesmans, Liam Vandekerckhove, Eric Beamish, Koen Ongena, Wouter Renckens, Pol Van Dorpe, Sanjin Marion

entry.summary: Investigates effective code-interpreter reasoning in LLMs from extrinsic (crucial tokens) and intrinsic (code-specific cognitive behaviors) perspectives, finding stronger models exhibit higher prevalence of both. Studies what behavioral properties underlie effective executable reasoning.

entry.title: Dynestyx: A Probabilistic Programming Library for Dynamical Systems

author.name: Daniel Waxman, Dmitry Batenkov, John Feser, Andy Zane, Eli Bingham, Youssef Marzouk, Matthew E. Levine

entry.summary: Introduces Dynestyx, a probabilistic programming library that adds first-class support for state-space models and dynamical systems, including state and parameter estimation. It aims to make advanced Bayesian methods more accessible to practitioners following the Bayesian workflow.

entry.title: Exploding and vanishing gradients in deep neural networks: the effect of residual connections

author.name: Vivek S Borkar

entry.summary: Analyzes exploding and vanishing gradients in deep networks using multiplicative ergodic theory and Lyapunov exponents, characterizing how residual connections affect the Lyapunov spectrum. It offers a rigorous theoretical explanation of a well-known empirical phenomenon.

entry.title: A Practical Evaluation Method for Long-Form Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Yulin Xue, Siqi Ouyang, Lei Li

entry.summary: Proposes a practical, reproducible evaluation method for long-form simultaneous speech-to-speech translation using ASR, forced alignment, and sentence-embedding matching to recover sentence-level metrics. It addresses gaps in evaluating continuous, unsegmented input.

entry.title: ROMPAR: Morphological Completion and Demographic Unlearning for Romanian-Accented Speech Recognition

author.name: Andrei-Marius Avram, Aureliu-Valentin Antonie, \c{S}tefan-Bogdan Badea, Andrei Florea, Robert-Nicolae Zaharoiu, Dumitru-Clementin Cercel

entry.summary: ROMPAR is a 17.8-hour Romanian and Moldavian parliamentary speech corpus with double annotation and labels for reconstructed word fragments, paired with a multi-task adversarial training framework enforcing demographic invariance. It includes an exponential decay mechanism to stabilize adversarial objectives.

entry.title: PaperJury: Due-Process Review for Bounded LaTeX Revision

author.name: Yiran Wang, Ruixuan An, Biao Wu, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: PaperJury is a closed-loop review-verdict-revise-verify system for pre-submission hardening of LaTeX CS papers, combining deterministic orchestration with semantic adjudication. It supports durable issue identity across rounds, no-fix outcomes, and artifact-safe bounded revision.

entry.title: The Art of Mixology: Mixup-based Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving Split Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Chen, Xiang Gao, Xianshun Wang, Chengran Li, Shengyu Xia, Xueluan Gong, Linru Zhang, Qian Wang, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: MIXGUARD proposes a mixup-based token-level obfuscation method for privacy-preserving split learning of LLMs, addressing the trade-off between utility, privacy, efficiency, and stability. It aims to resist data reconstruction attacks while keeping computation feasible for resource-constrained users.

entry.title: When the Same Musical Knowledge Forgets Differently: A Clean Probe of Pathway-Dependent Forgetting

author.name: Yu Liu, Zhiwei Yang, Wenxiao Zhang, Cong Cao, Fangfang Yuan, Kun Peng, Haimei Qin, Lei Jiang, Jin B. Hong, Hao Peng, Yanbing Liu

entry.summary: This paper tests the Pathway-Invariant Assumption by examining whether the acquisition route (listening vs reading) of the same musical knowledge affects how easily it is forgotten in multimodal models. Music understanding provides a clean controlled test where the same knowledge unit enters via audio or text.

entry.title: Interpolation between Convolution and Attention via K-Nearest Neighbors

author.name: Mingi Kang

entry.summary: This work unifies convolution and self-attention within a single k-nearest-neighbor aggregation framework, arguing both are special cases of neighbor selection and weighted aggregation. Convolution selects by spatial proximity while attention selects by feature similarity, placing them on a continuous spectrum.

entry.title: Text-Driven Fusion for Infrared and Visible Images: Achieving Image Scene Adaptation on Hyperbolic Space

author.name: Huan Kang, Hui Li, Tianyang Xu, Tao Zhou, Xiao-Jun Wu, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: This work introduces a text-driven infrared-visible image fusion framework using hyperbolic manifold learning, with BLIP text prompts as topological anchors guiding vision-attribute alignment. It exploits the Poincaré ball's negative curvature to embed coarse-to-fine semantic hierarchies.

entry.title: SGFormer++: Semantic Graph Transformer for Incremental 3D Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Mengshi Qi, Changsheng Lv, Zijian Fu, Xianlin Zhang, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: SGFormer++ is a Semantic Graph Transformer for incremental 3D scene graph generation that uses Transformer layers for global message passing, overcoming over-smoothing and limited receptive fields of GCN-based methods. It introduces an edge-aware Graph Embedding Layer with linear complexity.

entry.title: From Frames to Temporal Graphs: In-Context Egocentric Action Recognition with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bessie Dominguez-Dager, Francisco Gomez-Donoso, Miguel Cazorla, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Barath, Zuria Bauer

entry.summary: Converts egocentric videos into Temporal Action Graphs via a multi-stage prompting pipeline, decoupling visual perception from symbolic reasoning to enable in-context few-shot action recognition with VLMs. Shows gains over zero-shot frame baselines on EGTEA and Epic-Kitchens.

entry.title: An Extensive Benchmark for Single-round and Multi-round Instruction-based Image Editing

author.name: Yiwei Ma, Ke Ye, Weihuang Lin, Jiayi Ji, Xiaoshuai Sun, Tat-Seng Chua, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: Introduces I2EBench2.0, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating single-round and multi-round instruction-based image editing across diverse edit types. Provides standardized evaluation to guide future editing model development.

entry.title: Self-Questioning Vision-Language Models: Reinforcement Learning for Compositional Visual Reasoning

author.name: Saraswathy Amjith

entry.summary: A self-questioning framework trains a VLM via GRPO reinforcement learning to decompose visual questions into sub-questions and answer them sequentially, without human-written reasoning annotations. Improves compositional visual reasoning.

entry.title: TurboGS: Accelerating 3D Gaussian Splatting via Error-Guided Sparse Pixel Sampling and Optimization

author.name: Zheng Dong, Daifei Qiu, Pinxuan Dai, Ke Xu, Jiamin Xu, Lili He, Rynson W. H. Lau, Weiwei Xu

entry.summary: TurboGS accelerates 3D Gaussian Splatting training via error-guided sparse pixel sampling that concentrates optimization on perceptually informative pixels, plus a tile-wise structure-aware loss. Targets fast, high-fidelity novel-view rendering for consumer applications.

entry.title: Learning Directional Semantic Transitions for Longitudinal Chest X-ray Analysis

author.name: Zhangfeng Hu, Zefan Yang, Ge Wang, Tanveer Syeda-Mahmood, Anushree Burade, Mannudeep Kalra, Pingkun Yan

entry.summary: ProTrans is a vision-language pretraining framework for longitudinal chest X-ray analysis that models disease progression as a directional semantic transition between paired studies, anchored by radiology reports and a learnable progression feature map. Captures subtle, directional progression semantics.

entry.title: MMDiff: Extending Diffusion Transformers for Multi-Modal Generation

author.name: Yagmur Akarken, Orest Kupyn, Christian Rupprecht

entry.summary: MMDiff converts a frozen diffusion transformer into a multi-modal generative system that jointly produces images and dense perceptual modalities via lightweight decoder heads. Its key finding is that perceptual information is temporally distributed across the denoising trajectory, requiring multi-timestep feature fusion that boosts segmentation by up to 28.7% mIoU.

entry.title: Wavelength-Multiplexed 2D Beam Steering via a Passive Diffractive Network

author.name: Che-Yung Shen, Yuhang Li, Cagatay Isil, Tianyi Gan, Mona Jarrahi, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: This work introduces a passive diffractive optical network that maps illumination wavelength to programmable 2D beam steering using cascaded deep-learning-optimized diffractive layers. Unlike single-layer dispersive elements limited to 1D mapping, it achieves arbitrary 2D steering without mechanical scanning or electronic phase control.

entry.title: From Attacks to Curricula: Learnability-Guided Adversarial Training for Safe Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuewen Mei, Tong Nie, Jie Sun, Haotian Shi, Wei Ma, Jian Sun

entry.summary: AlignADV converts adversarial driving scenarios into capability-aligned curricula, avoiding the common pitfall where collision-driven generators produce unsolvable extreme cases that hurt learning. This improves sample efficiency and convergence in closed-loop adversarial training for autonomous driving safety.

entry.title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models

author.name: Ge Wang, Xinyu Tan, Xiang Li, Man Luo, Chengsi Yao, Shenhao Yan, Jiahao Yang, Fan Feng, Honghao Cai, Xiangyuan Wang, Zhixin Mai, Yiming Zhao, Yatong Han, Zhen Li

entry.summary: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning (EQRL) makes VLA policy execution adaptive by jointly selecting latent input, denoising budget, and action chunk length per query based on state difficulty, without fine-tuning the underlying model. It allocates more computation to contact-rich or uncertain states.

entry.title: Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Policy: Learning Precise and Robust Manipulation with a Single RGB Camera

author.name: Seoyoon Kim, Kanghyun Kim, Dongwoo Ko, Yeong Jin Heo, Min Jun Kim

entry.summary: Spatially Conditioned Diffusion Policy (SCDP) achieves precise single-RGB-camera manipulation by using predicted end-effector trajectories as visual attention anchors to identify task-relevant regions, avoiding the need for wrist-mounted cameras. It demonstrates robust manipulation from a single global view.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory-Routed Causal Memory for Delayed-Evidence Visuomotor Imitation

author.name: Zihao Li, Ranpeng Qiu, Yincong Chen, Guoqiang Ren, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: TRACE introduces a trajectory-routed causal memory for visuomotor imitation in delayed-evidence tasks, where an early cue disappears before a later decision, storing task-relevant evidence in bounded latent memory indexed by path state rather than time. It addresses partial observability in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Instruct-Particulate: Scaling Feed-Forward 3D Object Articulation with Kinematic Control

author.name: Ruining Li, Yuxin Yao, Matt Zhou, Chuanxia Zheng, Christian Rupprecht, Joan Lasenby, Shangzhe Wu, Andrea Vedaldi

entry.summary: Instruct-Particulate is a feed-forward model that takes a 3D mesh plus a kinematic specification (part descriptions, connectivity, joint types, optional point prompts) and predicts kinematic part segmentation and joint motion parameters. It addresses data scarcity in articulated 3D reconstruction for animation, gaming, and robotic simulation.

entry.title: Import AI 461: "Alignment is not on track"; FrontierCode; and synthetic research interns

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: An issue of Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter covering the launch of a new alignment nonprofit (Sequent) by researchers from UK AISI and Timaeus who argue alignment is not on track for superintelligence, plus FrontierCode and synthetic research interns. It synthesizes notable developments in AI safety and research.

entry.title: PrologMCP: A Standardized Prolog Tool Interface for LLM Agents

author.name: Agnieszka Mensfelt, Adarsh Prabhakaran, Adrian Haret, Vince Trencsenyi, Kostas Stathis

entry.summary: PrologMCP exposes Prolog as a stateful tool via the Model Context Protocol, enabling LLM agents to delegate deductive reasoning to a symbolic solver through a reusable translate-run-inspect-repair loop. Targets deep deductive tasks where LLMs fail.

entry.title: Frame-Conditioned Moral Computation in LLaMA 3.1-8B-Instruct: A Mechanistic Interpretability Audit of Ethical Reasoning

author.name: Ali Dasdan, Manan Shah, W. Russell Neuman, Chad Coleman, Kund Meghani, Safinah Ali

entry.summary: Performs a mechanistic interpretability audit of moral reasoning in LLaMA 3.1-8B-Instruct across 54 moral prompts using the Transluce platform, identifying a Situational Anchor Effect where domain-specific representations dominate activations. Examines internal computation rather than just behavior.

entry.title: UrbanWell: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Spatio-Temporal Urban Wellbeing Analytics

author.name: Yanxin Xi, Xiang Su, Jie Feng, Yu Liu, Sasu Tarkoma, Pan Hui

entry.summary: UrbanWell is a large-scale benchmark evaluating multimodal LLMs' spatio-temporal reasoning for urban wellbeing across 38 cities, jointly modeling satellite and street view imagery against environmental, accessibility, and urban-form indicators. Tests integration of heterogeneous spatial signals.

entry.title: Medical Heuristic Learning: An LLM-Driven Framework for Interpretable and Auditable Clinical Decision Rules

author.name: Wei Xu, Ke Yang, Gang Luo, Keli Zheng, Lingyan Hu, Jing Wang, Kefeng Li

entry.summary: Medical Heuristic Learning uses LLMs to derive interpretable, auditable clinical decision rules for tabular medical prediction under limited data, class imbalance, and feature evolution. Instantiates a learning-beyond-gradients paradigm to avoid black-box deep learning in clinical settings.

entry.title: RAID: Semantic Graph Diffusion for True Cold-Start and Cross-Lingual Forecasting

author.name: Arunkumar V, Manoranjan Gandhudi, Gangadharan G. R., Arun Prakash, S. Senthilkumar

entry.summary: RAID handles true cold-start forecasting (items with no history) using metadata-driven semantic retrieval and graph-conditioned diffusion, mapping textual metadata into a shared multilingual embedding space and refining neighbor-aggregated forecasts via gated diffusion. Extends naturally to unseen and cross-lingual items.

entry.title: MiroBench: Benchmarking Realism in Agentic Simulation of Real-world Discussions

author.name: Yaoning Yu, Ye Yu, Haojing Luo, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: MiroBench benchmarks whether LLM-agent simulations preserve the content patterns and interaction dynamics of real human discussions, using Reddit threads as a concrete grounded setting. Provides a unified evaluation to compare social-simulation systems and measure realism progress.

entry.title: GeoRoPE: Ground-Aware Rotary Adaptation for Remote Sensing Foundation Models

author.name: Yu Luo, Kun Hu, Mengwei He, Xiaogang Zhu, Shan Zeng, Allen Benter, Wei Xiang, Patrick Filippi, Thomas Francis Bishop, Zhiyong Wang

entry.summary: GeoRoPE is a ground-aware, RoPE-compatible, parameter-efficient spatial adaptation method for remote-sensing foundation models that recalibrates token-level positional interactions to resolve scale mismatch across sensors and ground sampling distances. Addresses physical inconsistency of fixed grid-based positional priors.

entry.title: XFlow: An Executable Protocol Programming System for Reliable Multi-Agent Workflows

author.name: Hanqi Li, Jing Peng, Zijian Wang, Lu Chen, Kai Yu

entry.summary: XFlow is an executable protocol programming system and accompanying DSL (XPF) for reliable multi-agent LLM workflows, addressing the underspecified prompt-harness boundary. It compiles literate protocols into executable structure to decide which commitments stay in prompts versus harness.

entry.title: JetParticle-JEPA: An Efficient Self-Supervised Representation Learning method for Jet Tagging in High-Energy Physics

author.name: Guillaume Letellier (LPCC), Antonin Vacheret (LPCC), Fr\'ed\'eric Jurie

entry.summary: JP-JEPA is a self-supervised joint-embedding predictive architecture for jet tagging in high-energy physics that learns from continuous particle clouds without tokenization or reconstruction. It matches supervised SOTA on JetClass while improving label efficiency and robustness.

entry.title: Rational Sparse Autoencoder

author.name: Naiyu Yin, Yue Yu

entry.summary: The Rational Sparse Autoencoder replaces fixed encoder nonlinearities (ReLU, JumpReLU, TopK) with a trainable rational function for mechanistic interpretability. The richer activation class can uniformly approximate existing SAE primitives while better adapting the reconstruction-sparsity trade-off.

entry.title: Beyond Scalar Distances: Semantic Attribute Gradients from Frozen MLLMs for Visual Embeddings

author.name: Shubhang Bhatnagar, Dheeraj Baiju, Narendra Ahuja

entry.summary: SAGA turns attribute-aware perception from a frozen multimodal LLM into a training signal for vision encoders, using GRPO to reward the MLLM for correct predictions on the encoder's tokens. This produces richer, attribute-aware embeddings beyond scalar class-label supervision for retrieval.

entry.title: Driving, Fast or Slow? Neuro-Symbolic Guidance for Motion Prediction in Multi-Modal Ground Mobility

author.name: Simon Kohaut, Felix Divo, Julius Hahnewald, Benedict Flade, Julian Eggert, Kristian Kersting, Devendra Singh Dhami

entry.summary: TraCS is a neuro-symbolic framework that augments black-box motion prediction backbones with interpretable probabilistic first-order logic encoding traffic regulations. It uses an agentic code-generation pipeline to translate natural-language traffic rules into probabilistic constraints for safer multi-modal trajectory prediction.

entry.title: AP-GRPO: Anchor-Gated Phonetic Alignment with Policy Optimization for Pathological Speech Reconstruction

author.name: Pengfei Zhang, Hoang H Nguyen, Yutong Song, Wenjun Huang, Tahmid Imtiaz Imu, Henry Peng Zou, Jiang Wu, Honghui Xu, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: AP-GRPO is a GRPO framework with phonetic rewards that reconstructs pathological speech by preserving audible anchor words and enforcing inter-anchor phonetic compatibility. Targets recovering intended text from distorted speech of neurodegenerative patients.

entry.title: When Generator Replay Degrades: Projected Rehearsal Orchestration for Heterogeneous Federated Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Thinh T. H. Nguyen, Khoa D. Doan, Binh T. Nguyen, Danh Le-Phuoc, Kok-Seng Wong

entry.summary: PRO replaces synthetic input replay with projected rehearsal orchestration for heterogeneous federated class-incremental learning, maintaining compact class-level projected memories on the server to mitigate forgetting under uneven, modality-varying task streams. Improves robustness over generator-replay approaches.

entry.title: Variance Reduction for Non-Log-Concave Sampling with Applications to Inverse Problems

author.name: M. Berk Sahin, Ahmet Ege Tanriverdi, Behzad Sharif, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: Develops the first unified analysis of variance-reduction estimators (momentum SGD, STORM, PAGE) for sampling from high-dimensional non-log-concave distributions with stochastic gradients. Establishes improved non-asymptotic convergence bounds with applications to inverse problems.

entry.title: The Proxy Knows Too Much: Sealing LLM API Routers with Attested TEEs

author.name: Sipeng Xie, Qianhong Wu, Hengrun Lu, Ziliang Sun, Qi Wu, Bo Qin, Qin Wang

entry.summary: Identifies LLM API routers as application-layer man-in-the-middle risks that can rewrite tool calls, swap dependencies, and exfiltrate secrets, then proposes AEGIS, an attested router confining plaintext handling to a hardware enclave with client-verified passthrough. Addresses evadable client-side defenses.

entry.title: Tyler: Typed Latent Reasoning for Language Models -- When to Think, What to Compute, and How Much to Allocate

author.name: Hanyu Lin, Min Cai, Jiawei Wen, Haodi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Tyler, a typed and budget-aware latent reasoning framework that decides when to invoke latent computation, what type to perform, and how much budget to allocate during decoding. Aims to reduce chain-of-thought redundancy and inference overhead via continuous representations.

entry.title: Automated jailbreak attack targeting multiple defense strategies

author.name: Qi Wang, Chengcheng Wan, Weijia He, Yanqing Li, Hanqi Sun, Xiaodong Gu, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: UNIATTACK is a defense-oriented black-box jailbreak framework that extracts minimal high-impact attack features from diverse existing attacks and composes them into flexible templates via an attacker LLM. It aims for one-shot effectiveness against multiple defense strategies.

entry.title: Compositional Reasoning Depth Predicts Clinical AI Failure: Empirical Evidence Consistent with Transformer Compositionality Limits in Electronic Health Record Question Answering

author.name: Sanjay Basu

entry.summary: This study introduces a hop-count taxonomy of reasoning steps as a predictor of LLM failure on electronic health record question answering, finding deeper compositional questions yield disproportionately more errors. It links empirical clinical AI failure to transformer compositionality limits.

entry.title: GRASP: Gradient-Aligned Sequential Parameter Transfer for Memory-Efficient Multi-Source Learning

author.name: Mary Isabelle Wisell, Nicholas Jacobs, Aayush Manandhar, Salimeh Yasaei Sekeh

entry.summary: GRASP is a multi-source transfer learning method that sequentially merges source models one at a time with gradient-aligned parameter selection, achieving O(1) memory while avoiding negative transfer. It removes the O(K) memory bottleneck of simultaneous model fusion.

entry.title: Physics-conforming Latent Twins

author.name: Matthias Chung, Yutong Bu, Deepanshu Verma

entry.summary: Physics-conforming Latent Twins learn latent surrogate solution operators whose dynamics satisfy selected physical principles like conservation laws and dissipative structures by design. It jointly learns encoder, decoder, and a latent flow map for reliable time-dependent surrogates.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Random Projection for Activation Steering in Language Models

author.name: Minh-Hieu Pham, Bach Do, Laziz Abdullaev, Tan Minh Nguyen, Khoat Than

entry.summary: HiDRA is a training-free activation steering method that performs activation addition in a randomly projected high-dimensional space to capture discriminative signals beyond what linear difference-in-means methods recover under the superposition hypothesis. It integrates with existing steering methods.

entry.title: Rethinking Structural Anomaly Detection: From Decision Boundaries to Projection Operators

author.name: Alexander Bauer

entry.summary: Reframes structural anomaly detection by learning a projection operator onto the manifold of normal samples and flagging points altered by the projection, rather than estimating densities or decision boundaries. This matches the inductive bias to low-dimensional manifold-supported data.

entry.title: MoECa: Aligning Feature Reuse with Expert Decomposition in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Maoliang Li, Haojing Chen, Jiayu Chen, Zihao Zheng, Xinhao Sun, Hailong Zou, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: MoECa is a fine-grained caching framework for Diffusion Transformers with Mixture-of-Experts that performs branch-level feature reuse across timesteps rather than token-level caching. It exploits cross-timestep redundancy at the expert-branch level with expert-aware adaptive control.

entry.title: Conflict-Aware Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Yijun Lu, Zihan Fang, Pengpeng Qiao, Zheng Lin, Jing Yang, Yuxin Zhang, Por Lip Yee, Zhe Chen, Jun Luo

entry.summary: FC-MoE is a conflict-aware federated fine-tuning method for MoE LLMs that addresses destructive interference when same-indexed experts optimize under conflicting client data distributions. It stabilizes aggregation under data heterogeneity in privacy-preserving collaborative settings.

entry.title: One-Step Generalization Ratio Guided Optimization for Domain Generalization

author.name: Sumin Cho, Dongwon Kim, Kwangsu Kim

entry.summary: GENIE is a domain-generalization optimizer that uses the One-Step Generalization Ratio to quantify each parameter's contribution to loss reduction and gradient alignment, then dynamically equalizes OSGR via preconditioning to avoid reinforcing spurious correlations. It ensures balanced parameter updates against domain-specific overfitting.

entry.title: SPICE: Synergy and Partial Information Based Curriculum Evolution

author.name: Ankush Pratap Singh, Houwei Cao, Yong Liu

entry.summary: SPICE is a multimodal curriculum learning framework that uses Partial Information Decomposition to decompose interactions into redundant, unique, and synergistic components, enabling dynamic adaptation as the model evolves. It addresses limitations of static curriculum assumptions.

entry.title: Continual Backdoor Training in IoT/CPS

author.name: Oxana Salish, Kuniyilh S

entry.summary: This paper formalizes an IoT/CPS-specific threat model and presents a backdoor attack that exploits continual learning's incremental updates, replay buffers, and representation reuse to implant persistent dormant behaviors. It highlights security vulnerabilities introduced by continual adaptation.

entry.title: DLWM: Diverse Latent World Models for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: David Huang, Lianlei Shan

entry.summary: DLWM proposes diverse latent world models for multimodal reasoning that maintain multiple plausible interpretations of ambiguous visual inputs rather than a single fixed reasoning path. It aims to improve hypothesis exploration while reducing memory and rollout costs.

entry.title: Structured Nonparametric Variational Inference for Dependent Latent Modeling

author.name: Yuda Shao, Zhiling Gu, Shan Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Structured Nonparametric Variational Inference (SN-VI) using multivariate splines to model dependencies among latent variables, moving beyond the mean-field assumption. Provides theoretical guarantees on the variational lower bound.

entry.title: Faithful Action-unit Causal Reasoning for Counterfactually Faithful Emotion Explanations

author.name: Van Thong Huynh, Hong Hai Nguyen, Thuy Pham, Trong Nghia Nguyen, Soo-Hyung Kim

entry.summary: Proposes FACR, which casts facial action-unit to emotion reasoning as a counterfactual-consistency problem against a structural causal graph, training a faithfulness objective so causal AUs move predictions and irrelevant ones do not. Aims to make emotion explanations faithful rather than merely plausible.

entry.title: GRACE-DS: a Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment in Data Science

author.name: Aleksandr Tsymbalov, Danis Zaripov, Artem Epifanov, Anastasya Palienko

entry.summary: Introduces GRACE-DS, a pre-deployment evaluation environment for LLM-powered AutoML agents on tabular tasks, with hidden validators measuring leakage avoidance, reproducibility, protocol validity, and correction behavior beyond final accuracy. Finds flexible iterative interaction yields the strongest results.

entry.title: GPT-Based Fast Simulation of CLAS12 Detector Hits via Conditional Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Cole Granger, James Giroux, Richard Tyson, Maurizio Ungaro, Cristiano Fanelli

entry.summary: Applies a GPT-style autoregressive transformer as a fast surrogate model for simulating calorimeter detector hits in the CLAS12 particle physics experiment, conditioned on incident momentum. Offers an LLM-inspired alternative to costly Monte-Carlo detector simulation.

entry.title: In-Domain Supervised Pathology Report Classification: A Reproducible Pipeline from Data Curation to Production-Matched Evaluation

author.name: Isaac Hands, Bin Huang, Adam Spannaus, John Gounley, Heidi Hanson, Eric Durbin, Sally R. Ellingson

entry.summary: Presents a reproducible in-domain supervised pipeline for pathology report classification that counters out-of-distribution drops when models move across cancer registries. It standardizes data curation with facility-stratified sampling and chooses operating points keeping false-negative rates low.

entry.title: From Argument Components to Graphs: A Multi-Agent Debate with Confidence Gating for Argument Relations

author.name: Jakub B\k{a}ba, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent debate framework with confidence gating using a Proponent-Opponent-Judge architecture to extract argument relations and build argument graphs without fine-tuning. It addresses self-correction reinforcing hallucinations in argument mining.

entry.title: Connecting Speech to Words through Images

author.name: Gabriel Pirlogeanu, Dan Oneata, Horia Cucu, Herman Kamper

entry.summary: The authors propose a visually grounded method to learn mappings between written and spoken words using only images and spoken descriptions, with no text supervision. They combine image captioning, utterance matching, and unsupervised word discovery for spoken word retrieval.

entry.title: SCAR: Semantic Continuity-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Context Expansion in RAG

author.name: Nathana\"el Langlois

entry.summary: SCAR is an adaptive retrieval policy for RAG that selectively expands neighboring chunks by weighing query-neighbor relevance against a structural continuity penalty, addressing boundary fragmentation from fixed chunking. It uses a scale-invariant relative expansion threshold that transfers across embedding models.

entry.title: Gaussian Spatial Priors for Anatomy-Aware Object Detection in Surgical Videos

author.name: Yunfan Li, Artem Shmelev, Himanshu Gupta

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Gaussian Spatial Prior module that encodes anatomically constrained spatial relationships as a parametric bias injected into the self-attention of a DAB-DETR decoder for surgical video object detection. It improves detection of small, intermittently visible structures like epigastric vessels.

entry.title: RefGC-SR$^2$: Reference-guided Generated Content Super-Resolution and Refinement

author.name: Jeahun Sung, Dahyeon Kye, Soo Ye Kim, Jihyong Oh

entry.summary: RefGC-SR2 jointly tackles reference-guided generated content super-resolution and refinement, addressing the limitation that high-resolution reference images are downsampled before generation, discarding fine detail. It corrects generation artifacts while recovering resolution beyond the low-resolution domain.

entry.title: Decoupled Motion Representation Learning for Moving Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Guoyi Zhang, Peiwen Wu, Han Wang, Xiangpeng Xu, Xiaohu Zhang

entry.summary: This work proposes decoupled motion representation learning for moving infrared small target detection, observing that background motions are globally coherent while small targets are sparse local anomalies. It separates these to reduce false alarms from coherent background dynamics.

entry.title: OneFocus: Enabling Real-World X-ray Security Screening with a Unified Vision-Language Model

author.name: Jiali Wen, Hongxia Gao, Litao Li, Yixin Chen, Kaijie Zhang, Qianyun Liu, Xiaoqin Wen

entry.summary: OneFocus is a unified vision-language model for real-world X-ray security screening, accompanied by MMXray (52k image-caption pairs over 28 contraband classes) and CleanDET, a synthesis dataset for realistic occlusion. Aims to bring VLM generalization to contraband detection.

entry.title: CRIS: Cross-Plane Self-Supervised Isotropic Restoration for Anisotropic Volumetric Imaging Across Modalities

author.name: Adi Ahituv, Anat Ilivitzki, Moti Freiman

entry.summary: CRIS is a cross-plane self-supervised framework for isotropic restoration of anisotropic volumetric MRI and electron microscopy without paired ground truth, casting 3D restoration as 2D stripe completion on orthogonal reformats. Generalizes across modalities.

entry.title: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Visual Grounding for Remote Sensing Images and Videos

author.name: Ke Li, Di Wang, Yongshan Zhu, Ting Wang, Weiping Ni, Tao Lei, Quan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: RSVG-ZeroOV is a training-free framework for open-vocabulary visual grounding in remote sensing images and videos, leveraging frozen foundation models in an Overview-Focus-Evolve paradigm. Avoids costly task-specific annotations while generalizing to novel objects and relations.

entry.title: Training-free sparse attention based on cumulative energy filtering

author.name: Chunlu Li, Yixuan Pan, Bai Du, Zhenyuan Chen, Yanzhao Li, Hui Dong, Hui Wang, Zhiqiang Zou

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free sparse attention method for Diffusion Transformers in video generation that filters tokens by cumulative energy, framing token selection as dual-goal optimization of sparsity and accuracy. Argues a fixed recall rate ensures accuracy while a fixed threshold is suboptimal for cost.

entry.title: Look Again Before You Abstain:Budgeted Conformal Evidence Acquisition for Reliable Vision-Language Model

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: BCEA addresses LVLM hallucination via selective prediction with distribution-free guarantees, showing that conformal filtering to keep hallucination under 5% forces abstention on over 80% of claims. It replaces binary answer/abstain with budgeted acquisition of additional visual evidence to reduce wasteful abstention.

entry.title: Scalable Dynamic Tactile Sensing Enabled by Passive and Flexible Acoustic Waveguides

author.name: Guimin Long, Changhong Linghu, Chuanping Liu, Ke Xu, Xingjian Jing
